Yet the Servant also knows the taste of failure: “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my cause is with the LORD.” God's answer is astonishing. Instead of reducing the mission, he enlarges it: “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob… I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.” On Tuesday of Holy Week we hear this as the prayer of Jesus. To human eyes his work in Jerusalem is collapsing; one of the Twelve is about to sell him, another will deny him, the rest will run. Yet through that apparent failure the light will reach the whole world, even to the shores of India. The Psalm is the prayer of one who has trusted God from the womb: “Upon you I have leaned from my birth.”

The Gospel takes us into the Upper Room. Jesus has just washed the feet of the disciples, and now he is “troubled in spirit” and says: “Very truly, I tell you, one of you will betray me.” The disciples look at one another. The beloved disciple, reclining next to Jesus, asks: “Lord, who is it?” Jesus dips a piece of bread and gives it to Judas. In the East, to give a morsel from the dish to a guest was a sign of honour and friendship. Even at this moment Jesus offers Judas love. But Judas takes the bread and goes out. St John adds four words that fall like a stone: “And it was night.” Not only the night outside, but the night of a heart that refuses the light. And yet Jesus says: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified.” The hour of betrayal is also the hour of glory, because love is about to be shown to the end.

Then Peter speaks with all his warm, impulsive heart: “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.” Jesus answers gently and truly: “Will you lay down your life for me? Very truly, I tell you, before the cock crows, you will have denied me three times.” Two disciples fail the Lord on the same night. The difference between them is not the size of their sin, but what they do afterwards. Judas goes out into the night and despairs. Peter will meet the gaze of Jesus, weep bitterly, and return (Luke 22:61–62). Jesus had said, “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but you will follow afterward”; and Peter did follow, to Rome and to his own cross. Holy Week is the time to be honest about our betrayals and denials, and to choose Peter's tears instead of Judas's night. No one is too far gone for the mercy of the One who gave the morsel even to his betrayer.
conn: The second Servant Song.
Isaiah 49:1–6. Paul and Barnabas quote verse 6 to explain their mission to the Gentiles (Acts 13:47): the Servant's light passes to the Church.
Reclining at table.
At a festive meal guests lay on cushions around a low table, leaning on the left elbow. The beloved disciple, at the right of Jesus, could lean back against his chest to ask him privately.
The morsel.
The host's gift of a piece of bread dipped in the dish was a mark of special favour. Psalm 41:9 stands behind the scene: “one who ate of my bread has lifted the heel against me” (John 13:18).
And it was night.
In John's Gospel light and darkness are always more than time of day (John 1:5; 3:19; 8:12). Nicodemus came by night and moved towards the light; Judas goes out into the night.
Cockcrow.
The Romans called the third watch of the night, from midnight to three, “cockcrow” (Mark 13:35). By dawn Peter will have denied his Lord.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
And it was night: and he who went out was himself the night. He went out from the light of the world into darkness, because he chose to love darkness rather than light.
St Ambrose (in substance)
Peter wept, and I do not read what he said; I read that he wept. Tears wash away the sin which the voice is ashamed to confess. Peter wept bitterly so that he might wash away his fault with tears.
outline: Ask: when have you failed someone you loved, and what did you do next?
The Servant's mission and his sense of failure.
Point 2 · A light to the nations
“I will give you as a light to the nations.”
live: Look at your apparent failures (Isaiah 49:4)
Offer to God one work that seems to have been in vain, and leave the result to him.
Choose the light
Bring to confession this week the sin you are most tempted to hide in the night.
Pray for someone who has left
Pray by name for one person who has left the Church or the faith, that they may come back like Peter.
2027-03-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were called from the womb to be a light to the nations, and in the night of betrayal you went on loving to the end. When we fail you, do not let us go out into the night like Judas, but look at us as you looked at Peter, so that we may weep, return and follow you. Make your salvation reach to the ends of the earth. Amen.
altar: In the Upper Room Jesus gave a morsel even to the one who would betray him. At the altar he gives himself to sinners again; let us receive him not with Judas's heart but with Peter's repentant love.

2027-03-24.title: Wednesday of Holy Week
readings: I did not hide my face from insult and spitting (Third Song of the Servant)
Lord, in your great love, answer me
The Son of Man goes as it is written of him, but woe to that one by whom the Son of Man is betrayed
2027-03-24.alt: Holy Week. Lent continues until the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper on Thursday. No Gloria, no Alleluia. Liturgical colour: violet. Traditionally called Spy Wednesday, from the bargain of Judas. This is the last full day of Lent; the Easter Triduum begins tomorrow evening. Some parishes keep Tenebrae tonight.
2027-03-24.verse: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame.
theo: The third Song of the Servant is the song of a disciple. “The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens, wakens my ear to listen as those who are taught.” Before the Servant speaks, he listens; every morning he lets God open his ear. Because he listens, he does not turn back when suffering comes: “I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out the beard; I did not hide my face from insult and spitting.” His strength is not hardness but trust: “The Lord GOD helps me… therefore I have set my face like flint.” We heard this same reading on Palm Sunday; today it prepares us for the night of Thursday and the day of Friday, when Jesus will be struck, mocked and spat upon, and will not hide his face. The Psalm is the cry of the righteous sufferer whom even his own family treats as a stranger: “It is zeal for your house that has consumed me… for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.” The Gospels saw this psalm fulfilled on Calvary (John 2:17; 19:28–29).

The Gospel tells the bargain. Judas goes to the chief priests and asks: “What will you give me if I betray him to you?” They pay him thirty pieces of silver. That was the price of a slave in the Law (Exodus 21:32), and the “lordly price” at which the shepherd of Zechariah was valued (Zechariah 11:12–13). From this bargain the day takes its old name in English, Spy Wednesday. Then the scene moves to preparation: “Where do you want us to make the preparations for you to eat the Passover?” Jesus is not a victim caught by surprise. He says: “My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.” He walks freely into his hour.

At table he says: “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.” And each disciple asks, “Surely not I, Lord?” That is the right question for us too. None of the Eleven was sure of himself; each knew that his heart could fail. Judas also asks, but notice the difference: the others say “Lord”; he says “Rabbi”, teacher. Jesus answers, “You have said so,” leaving the door open even now. The words of Jesus about Judas are solemn: “woe to that one by whom the Son of Man is betrayed!” They are not a curse but a lament, the grief of a friend. The Church does not pretend to know the final state of any soul; she knows that despair was Judas's last and greatest tragedy, and that no betrayal is greater than the mercy of Christ. On this last day before the Triduum, let us ask with the apostles, “Surely not I, Lord?”, and then run to the One who is about to give his life for betrayers, deniers and deserters, which is to say, for all of us.
conn: The third Servant Song.
Isaiah 50:4–9 (the Lectionary stops at 9a). The Servant is first a disciple, one who listens “as those who are taught.” The Song is read on Palm Sunday and again today.
Thirty pieces of silver.
The compensation for a slave gored by an ox (Exodus 21:32). Matthew sees Zechariah's “thirty shekels of silver” fulfilled (Matthew 27:9–10).
Spy Wednesday.
An old English name for this day, after Judas, who from this day watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over. In some lands the day is still marked by Tenebrae.
The first day of Unleavened Bread.
The Passover lamb was sacrificed on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that evening; for seven days no leaven was eaten (Exodus 12:15–20).
Rabbi and Lord.
In Matthew the faithful disciples call Jesus “Lord”; only Judas calls him “Rabbi” at the Supper and in Gethsemane (Matthew 26:25, 49).
Tenebrae.
Latin for darkness. A service of psalms and lamentations in which candles are put out one by one until the church is dark; a loud noise at the end recalls the earthquake at the death of Christ.
fathers: St Leo the Great (in substance)
Judas, more wicked than all, did not repent and seek pardon; had he not hastened to the noose, he could have obtained mercy. His despair, not only his betrayal, was his ruin.
St John Chrysostom (in substance)
See the gentleness of the Lord: even at the table he did not name the traitor before all, but gave him room to repent. He washed his feet and shared his bread, and still Judas did not turn back.
outline: Ask: what is a friendship worth? What would make someone sell it?
Morning by morning he wakens my ear.
He did not hide his face from insult.
The humble question of the disciple.
“The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced.”
live: Listen morning by morning (Isaiah 50:4)
Tomorrow morning, before your phone, read the Gospel of the day in silence for ten minutes.
Examine your price
Ask: for what do I betray Jesus? Money, comfort, the opinion of others? Name it and give it up for the Triduum.
Prepare the Passover
Prepare your home and your heart for the Triduum: clean, decide the family's times, and plan to keep Good Friday's fast.
2027-03-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, Servant who listened morning by morning, you set your face like flint and did not hide it from insult and spitting. You were sold for thirty pieces of silver by a friend. Keep us from selling you for any price. Let us ask humbly, Surely not I, Lord?, and run to your mercy. Bring us with you into these holy days. Amen.
altar: The one who was sold for thirty pieces of silver gives himself to us freely at the altar. What Judas sold, the Church receives as pure gift.

2027-03-29.title: Monday within the Octave of Easter
readings: This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses
Keep me safe, O God; you are my hope (or: Alleluia)
Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me
2027-03-29.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-29.verse: Suddenly Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!” And they came to him, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
theo: The Church does not celebrate Easter for one day only. For eight days, the Octave, she lives each day as if it were Easter Sunday: the Gloria is sung, the Alleluia rings out, and each day's readings show us a new appearance of the risen Lord. The early Christians called this week the week of the white garments, because the newly baptized wore their white robes every day until the following Sunday. Today Peter stands up on the day of Pentecost with the Eleven and speaks to the crowd in Jerusalem. He speaks of “Jesus of Nazareth, a man attested to you by God with deeds of power, wonders, and signs.” He was handed over and crucified, “But God raised him up, having freed him from death, because it was impossible for him to be held in its power.” Then Peter reads Psalm 16, today's Psalm, as a prophecy: David sang, “you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.” But David died and was buried, and his tomb is still there. So he was speaking of the Messiah. “This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses.”

Notice what has happened to Peter. A few weeks earlier he was so afraid that he denied Jesus before a servant girl. Now he stands before thousands and speaks with boldness. Nothing explains that change except what he says: he has seen the Lord alive, and he has received the Holy Spirit. The Resurrection is not only proven by an empty tomb; it is proven by transformed lives. Peter's courage, the joy of the martyrs, the faith that spread to the ends of the earth, including the shores of Kerala, all flow from that first morning. The Psalm gives words to this new confidence: “I keep the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my soul rejoices; my body also rests secure.”

In the Gospel the women leave the tomb “quickly with fear and great joy” and run to tell the disciples. Fear and joy together: that is often how Easter faith begins. And on the way, “suddenly Jesus met them.” He greets them simply, as a friend would. They take hold of his feet, real feet, and worship him. He says: “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers.” He calls the disciples who abandoned him “my brothers.” The Resurrection is reconciliation. Matthew then tells of a different response. Some of the guards report to the chief priests, who pay them to say that the disciples stole the body while they were asleep. Matthew records this because, in his own time, this story was circulating as an explanation of the empty tomb. It is not a judgement on the Jewish people; it is a reminder that every age offers its own ways of explaining the Resurrection away. St Augustine asked with a smile: if the guards were asleep, how did they know who took the body? The truth cannot be bought. The empty tomb stands, the witnesses speak, and the Lord meets us still on the road with his greeting: do not be afraid.
conn: The Octave of Easter.
The eight days from Easter Sunday to the Second Sunday of Easter are celebrated as one great day. Each day ranks as a solemnity; no memorials of saints are kept.
Week of the white garments.
The newly baptized wore their white garments all week and laid them aside on the following Sunday, once called “Sunday in white” (Dominica in albis).
Peter's speech.
Acts places this speech on the day of Pentecost. The Church reads it in the Easter Octave because it is the first public proclamation of the Resurrection.
David's tomb.
Peter points out that David's tomb was still known in Jerusalem (Acts 2:29). Psalm 16 could not be fully true of David; it is fulfilled in the Messiah, whose body did not see corruption.
Fear and great joy.
Matthew 28:8. Holy fear before the power of God, and overflowing joy at the good news: the right response to Easter.
“My brothers.”
For the first time in Matthew, Jesus calls the disciples his brothers (Matthew 28:10). The risen Lord restores the friendship they had broken.
The guards' story.
Matthew 28:11–15 answers a rumour of his own day. The Church reads it without hostility to the Jewish people (Nostra Aetate 4).
Galilee.
Where the call began. The risen Lord sends his disciples back to the place of their first love, to begin again.
altar: The women took hold of the feet of the risen Jesus. At the altar we receive the same risen Lord, not as a memory but as a living presence, in his true Body and Blood.
Today's collect prays that we may hold fast in our lives to the Sacrament we received in faith. Each Communion is a meeting on the road with the One who says: do not be afraid.
outline: Ask: what changed Peter from a coward into a fearless preacher?
Point 1 · Not abandoned to the grave
Psalm 16 fulfilled in the risen Christ.
The women run and meet the Lord.
Point 3 · The lie and the truth
The empty tomb cannot be explained away.
Women holding the feet of the risen Jesus.
“Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers.”
live: Run with the good news (Matthew 28:8)
Tell one person today, simply, that Christ is risen and what that means for you.
Keep the Lord before you (Psalm 16:8)
Begin each day of this Octave with a short prayer: “Lord, I keep you always before me.”
Call a brother back
Like Jesus who called the disciples “my brothers,” reach out to someone you have drifted from.
Pray for the newly baptized
Pray each day this week for those baptized at Easter, that they may hold fast to the faith.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)

The guards were told to say that the disciples stole the body while they slept. O wretched cunning! You bring forward sleeping witnesses. If they were asleep, what could they see? If they saw nothing, what is their testimony worth?
St Leo the Great (in substance)
The days between the Resurrection and the Ascension were not spent idly: in them great mysteries were confirmed and great truths revealed, so that our faith might rest on certainty and not on fear.
St Peter Chrysologus (in substance)
The women run, carrying the joy of the Resurrection. The Lord meets them on the way and greets them, so that the mouth of woman, through which death once entered, might now announce life.
magis: Catechism 639–644
The appearances of the risen Christ and the testimony of the witnesses.
Catechism 632–635
Christ was not abandoned to the realm of the dead; his body did not see corruption (Acts 2:27).
Catechism 1166–1167
Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, and the Easter Octave.
Lumen Gentium 35
The laity as witnesses to the Resurrection, proclaiming Christ by the testimony of their lives.
Nostra Aetate 4
Scripture is not to be read so as to blame the Jewish people.
saints: The holy women
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, Salome, Joanna and the other women who followed Jesus from Galilee were the first witnesses of the empty tomb and the first to meet the risen Lord.
This week

The Octave of Easter continues until Sunday 4 April, Divine Mercy Sunday. 2 Apr (St Francis of Paola) and other memorials are not kept during the Octave. 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred).
2027-03-29.prayer: O God, who give constant increase to your Church by new offspring, grant that your servants may hold fast in their lives to the Sacrament they have received in faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Risen Lord Jesus, you met the women on the road and said: do not be afraid. Meet us today on our roads. Turn our fear into joy, make us bold witnesses like Peter, and call back to you all our brothers and sisters who have wandered away. Alleluia. Amen.

2027-03-30.title: Tuesday within the Octave of Easter
readings: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ
The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord (or: Alleluia)
2027-03-30.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-30.verse: Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
theo: Peter's first Easter sermon reaches its climax: “God has made him both Lord and Messiah, this Jesus whom you crucified.” The listeners are “cut to the heart” and ask the question every converted heart asks: “Brothers, what should we do?” Peter's answer is the shape of Christian beginnings to this day: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” Repentance, Baptism, forgiveness, the Spirit. And the promise is wide: “for you, for your children, and for all who are far away, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to him.” That day about three thousand were added. Peter is not accusing a nation; he is speaking to the people in front of him, as the Church speaks to every one of us, for all of us by our sins had a part in the Lord's death (Catechism 598). The words “this Jesus whom you crucified” are addressed to me. And the same words carry mercy: the One we crucified is the One who forgives.

This Octave the Church remembers the many who were baptized at Easter all over the world. The Psalm is their song and ours: “Truly the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love, to deliver their soul from death.” “The earth is full of the steadfast love of the LORD.” The newly baptized have been cut to the heart, have turned to Christ, and now begin their life in the Spirit. In the early Church they received special instructions during this week, called mystagogy, explaining the sacraments they had just received. Every Christian can use this week to rediscover his own Baptism: the water, the oil, the white garment, the candle, the name.

In the Gospel Mary Magdalene stands weeping outside the tomb. She bends down and sees two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and one at the feet, like the cherubim over the ark of the covenant. “Woman, why are you weeping?” “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.” She turns and sees Jesus but does not recognize him; she thinks he is the gardener. In a way he is: the new Adam in the garden of the new creation. He asks: “Whom are you looking for?” Then he says one word: “Mary!” And she knows him. The Good Shepherd calls his own sheep by name, and they know his voice. She cries: “Rabbouni!” and clings to him. Jesus says: “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers.” Her love must now become mission; he will be present to her in a new way, no longer to be held as before, but to be shared. And so she goes: “I have seen the Lord.” The Church calls her “apostle to the apostles.” Like her, we too are called by name in Baptism, and we too are sent.
conn: Cut to the heart.
Acts 2:37. The Greek speaks of a sharp piercing. The word of God goes deeper than a reproach: it wounds in order to heal (Hebrews 4:12).
Three thousand.
Acts 2:41. At Sinai, after the golden calf, about three thousand died (Exodus 32:28); at the new Pentecost about three thousand receive new life.
Two angels.

Seated at the head and the foot, they recall the two cherubim facing each other over the mercy seat of the ark (Exodus 25:18–22): the empty place of the body has become the new place of God's presence.
The gardener.
Jesus was buried in a garden (John 19:41). Mary's mistake hides a truth: Easter is the new creation, and Christ the new Adam walks again in the garden.
“Mary!”
Jesus said the sheep know the shepherd's voice, and he calls them by name (John 10:3). One word reveals him.
“Do not hold on to me.”
Not a rejection: Jesus teaches that he will now be with his disciples in a new way, through his Ascension and the gift of the Spirit, in the sacraments and in the Church.
Apostle to the apostles.
An ancient title for Mary Magdalene (used by St Thomas Aquinas and others). In 2016 Pope Francis raised her memorial on 22 July to a feast.
Mystagogy.
The period after Baptism, especially the Easter season, in which the newly baptized are led deeper into the mysteries they have received (Catechism 1075).
altar: Mary was not allowed to hold on to Jesus as before; today he gives himself to be received in a new way, in the Eucharist, the gift of the risen Lord who has gone to the Father.
At each Mass the risen Christ calls us by name, and we go out from the altar, like Mary, to say: I have seen the Lord.
outline: Ask: how does it feel when someone who loves you calls your name?
A weeping woman turning at the sound of her name.
live: Remember your Baptism
Find out your baptismal day and your godparents' names; thank God, and if possible thank them.
Let God's word cut to the heart
Ask, as the crowd did: “What should I do?” and act on what God shows you.
Listen for your name
Spend ten minutes in silence today and let the Lord call you by name.
Share what you have seen
Like Mary Magdalene, tell someone one way the risen Lord has touched your life.
fathers: St Gregory the Great (in substance)
Mary sought and did not find; she persevered in seeking, and so she found. Holy desires grow by delay. Jesus said: Mary. He called her by name, as if to say: recognize him who recognizes you.
St Augustine (in substance)

“Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father.” Touch me by faith when I have ascended: that is, believe that I am equal to the Father. For a woman's hand to touch him was little; the heart's faith reaches him.
St Hippolytus of Rome (attributed, in substance)
The women became apostles to the apostles, sent by Christ. Eve's disobedience was undone by their obedience, and the first announcement of life came through the lips of women.
magis: Catechism 641
Mary Magdalene and the holy women, the first messengers of the Resurrection to the Apostles.
Catechism 1226–1228
Baptism from the day of Pentecost: Peter's call to repent and be baptized.
Catechism 1262–1266
The effects of Baptism: forgiveness of sins and new birth in the Holy Spirit.
Mulieris Dignitatem 16
St John Paul II on Mary Magdalene, “apostle of the apostles,” and the dignity of women in the Easter mystery.
Catechism 659–660
Christ's risen body and the Ascension: “Do not hold on to me.”
saints: St Mary Magdalene
Freed by Jesus from seven demons (Luke 8:2), she followed him to the cross and was the first to see him risen. Feast: 22 July.
This week
The Octave of Easter continues; each day is a solemnity. 4 Apr: Divine Mercy Sunday. 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred from 25 March).
2027-03-30.prayer: O God, who have bestowed on us paschal remedies, endow your people with heavenly gifts, so that, possessed of perfect freedom, they may rejoice in heaven over what gladdens them now on earth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Risen Lord, you called Mary by name and turned her tears into joy. Call us by name today. Cut us to the heart and draw us to repentance, renew in us the grace of our Baptism, and send us to our brothers and sisters to say: I have seen the Lord. Alleluia. Amen.

2027-03-31.title: Wednesday within the Octave of Easter
readings: What I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk
Rejoice, O hearts that seek the Lord (or: Alleluia)
They recognized him in the breaking of the bread
2027-03-31.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-31.verse: When he was at the table with them, he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.
theo: Peter and John go up to the Temple at three o'clock in the afternoon, the hour of prayer. They still pray as faithful Jews, in the Temple of their fathers. At the gate called Beautiful sits a man lame from birth, carried there every day to beg. He looks at them expecting a coin. Peter fixes his eyes on him: “Look at us.” Then he says the words that have become a motto for the Church's mission: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.” Peter takes him by the right hand and raises him up, and at once his feet and ankles are made strong. He jumps up, stands, walks, and enters the Temple with them, “walking and leaping and praising God.” Isaiah had promised that in the day of salvation “the lame shall leap like a deer.” The risen Lord is at work through his Church. Peter has no money, but he has the name of Jesus, and that is worth more than all the gold in the Temple. The Psalm sings: “Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.”

The Gospel is one of the most beloved pages of the New Testament: the road to Emmaus. On the evening of Easter Sunday two disciples, one named Cleopas, are walking about seven miles from Jerusalem, talking about everything that has happened. Jesus himself comes near and walks with them, “but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.” He asks what they are discussing, and they stand still, “looking sad.” Their words are heartbreaking: “we had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel.” Hope in the past tense. They even report the women's news of the empty tomb and the angels, but it has not reached their hearts. Then Jesus speaks: “Oh, how foolish you are, and how slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have declared! Was it not necessary that the Messiah should suffer these things and then enter into his glory?” And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interprets to them the things about himself in all the Scriptures. Later they will say: “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road?”

As they near the village he walks ahead as if he were going on. They urge him: “Stay with us, because it is almost evening.” He goes in. At table “he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them.” These are the same four actions as at the Last Supper and as at every Mass. “Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.” He is not gone; he is now present in a new way, in the bread broken and given. At once, though it is night, they get up and return to Jerusalem, where they hear: “The Lord has risen indeed, and he has appeared to Simon!” And they tell “how he had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread.” The road to Emmaus has the very shape of the Mass: the Lord walks with us in our sadness, explains the Scriptures in the Liturgy of the Word, makes himself known in the breaking of the bread in the Liturgy of the Eucharist, and sends us back on mission. “Breaking of the bread” was one of the first names Christians gave to the Eucharist (Acts 2:42). Every Sunday the risen Lord does for us exactly what he did at Emmaus.
conn: The ninth hour.
Three in the afternoon, the time of the evening sacrifice and prayer in the Temple (Acts 3:1). It is also the hour when Jesus died.
The Beautiful Gate.
Probably the great bronze Nicanor Gate leading into the Court of the Women. The lame man sat outside; now he enters, walking and leaping.
“In the name of Jesus.”
In the Bible the name stands for the person and his power. Peter heals not by his own power but by the authority of the risen Lord (Acts 3:12–16).
Emmaus.
A village about sixty stadia (about seven miles or eleven kilometres) from Jerusalem. Several places claim the site; the exact location is uncertain.
Cleopas.

Named only here. An early tradition (Hegesippus, recorded by Eusebius) speaks of a Clopas as brother of St Joseph; John 19:25 mentions “Mary the wife of Clopas.” The identification is possible but not certain.
“We had hoped.”
The saddest words in Luke 24:21. The Emmaus story is the story of hope given back.
Four actions.
Took, blessed, broke, gave: as at the feeding of the five thousand (Luke 9:16), the Last Supper (Luke 22:19) and every Eucharist.
“The breaking of the bread.”
An early Christian name for the Eucharist (Acts 2:42; Catechism 1329).
altar: At Emmaus the Lord was known in the breaking of the bread. At every Mass the same risen Christ takes, blesses, breaks and gives, and is truly present in the bread that is his Body.
The two disciples ran back to Jerusalem at night. Communion is never the end of the road: it sends us back to our brothers and sisters to say, the Lord is risen.
outline: Ask: have you ever walked away from Jerusalem, away from hope?
Point 1 · What I have I give you
Point 2 · Hearts burning on the road
Point 3 · Known in the breaking of bread
A small table at dusk, bread broken, and an empty chair.
“Stay with us, because it is almost evening.”
live: Give what you have
Like Peter, you may have no silver or gold; give time, a kind word or a prayer in Jesus' name to someone in need today.
Let your heart burn
Read Luke 24:13–35 slowly tonight, and ask the Lord to open the Scriptures to you.
Invite him in
Say before supper tonight: “Stay with us, Lord, because it is almost evening.”
Go back to Jerusalem
If you have drifted from the Church community, take one step back this week: a Sunday Mass, a parish group, a call to the priest.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)

Where did the Lord wish to be recognized? In the breaking of bread. We are sure: we break bread and we recognize the Lord. He did not want to be recognized anywhere else, for the sake of us who would not see him in the flesh but would eat his flesh.
St Gregory the Great (in substance)

They did not know him while he spoke of the Scriptures, but they knew him when he was fed at their table. Being hospitable to the stranger, they found God. Let us love hospitality, so that we may be received into the eternal dwellings.
St Ambrose (in substance)
Peter had no gold, but he had Christ; he had no silver, but he gave what is more precious than silver: health and the name of the Lord.
magis: Catechism 1329
The names of the Eucharist, including “the Breaking of Bread.”
Catechism 1346–1347
The Eucharist and the Emmaus meal: Word and Bread, as in every Mass.
Mane Nobiscum Domine 1–3 (St John Paul II, 2004)
“Stay with us, Lord”: the Emmaus icon of the Eucharist.
Dei Verbum 21
The Church has always venerated the Scriptures as she venerates the Body of the Lord, receiving the bread of life from the one table of God's word and Christ's Body.
Catechism 547–550
Signs of the Kingdom: the healings that continue in the name of Jesus.
saints: St Cleopas
Disciple of the Lord, one of the two who met him on the road to Emmaus; the Roman Martyrology commemorates him on 25 September.
This week
The Octave of Easter continues: Thursday, Friday and Saturday within the Octave. 4 Apr: Second Sunday of Easter (Divine Mercy). 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred from 25 March).
2027-03-31.prayer: O God, who gladden us year by year with the solemnity of the Lord's Resurrection, graciously grant that, by celebrating these present festivities, we may be worthy through them to reach eternal joys. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Stay with us, Lord, for it is almost evening. Walk with us when we are sad, open the Scriptures to us until our hearts burn, make yourself known to us in the breaking of the bread, and send us back with joy to tell our brothers and sisters that you are risen. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: God sent his people home from exile because he had compassion on them.
As Moses lifted up the serpent, the Son of Man is lifted up on the cross for our healing.
God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, not to condemn but to save.
2027-03-07.action: Learn John 3:16 by heart and pray it each morning this week.
2027-03-07.question: Do I prefer the darkness in some area of my life, and what would it take to come to the light?
catechism: Christ came not to condemn but to save.
Grace, the free gift of God.
kidsaint: Sts Perpetua and Felicity

Two brave young mothers who loved Jesus very much, long ago in Africa. One was a rich lady and the other was a servant, but in prison they became like sisters. They did not stop believing in Jesus, even when it was very hard. Lesson: friends who love Jesus make each other brave.
2027-03-07.special: Fourth Sunday of Lent (Laetare). Rose vestments may be worn. Second Scrutiny of the elect; the Year A readings may be used where there are catechumens.
term: Laetare
Latin for “rejoice,” the first word of the Entrance Antiphon of the Fourth Sunday of Lent (Isaiah 66:10). A day of quiet joy in the middle of Lent, when rose vestments may be worn.

family.explain: Jesus said: God loves the whole world so much that he gave us his only Son, Jesus. Whoever believes in him will live forever with God. God did not send Jesus to punish the world, but to save it. That is why we can be happy, even in Lent!
family.intention: We pray for people who feel that God is angry with them, that they may know his love.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we all learn John 3:16 by heart this week and say it together at night prayer?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital in Kozhikode a young nurse was assigned to an old man who shouted at everyone. One night she found him awake, staring at the small crucifix she wore. He asked why she wore it. She said: because when I am tired and angry I look at it, and I remember that someone loved me when I was not lovable. He was quiet for a long time. The next morning he asked to see a priest. He said: I want to look at that cross too.

pm.open: Father rich in mercy, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son. Draw us into his light. Amen.
share: By the rivers of Babylon… we wept when we remembered Zion (Psalm 137:1). Where do I feel in exile from God?
So must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). What wound do I need to bring to the cross?
People loved darkness rather than light (John 3:19). What am I keeping in the dark?
pm.resp: Let my tongue be silenced if I ever forget you!
interc: For the elect at their Second Scrutiny, that Christ may open their eyes to the light of faith.
For refugees and exiles who weep far from home, that they may find welcome and a way home.
For those who think they are beyond God's love, that they may look on the cross and live.
For rulers, that like Cyrus they may serve the good of peoples.
For our group, that we may rejoice in God's mercy and live in the light.
pm.close: Father, you did not send your Son to condemn but to save. Make us children of the light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God promises a new covenant written on our hearts, with sins forgiven.
Jesus says: unless a grain of wheat dies, it remains alone; if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Lifted up on the cross, Jesus draws all people to himself.
2027-03-14.action: Choose one hidden act of self-giving each day this week, and offer it as a grain of wheat.
2027-03-14.question: What in me needs to die so that Christ can bear fruit?
catechism: The New Law written on the heart.
The prayer of Jesus with loud cries and tears.
Lifted up, he draws all to himself.
kidsaint: St Patrick

As a boy in Britain he was captured by pirates and taken as a slave to Ireland, where he looked after sheep and learned to pray many times a day. He escaped, became a priest and bishop, and went back to the land of his captors to tell them about Jesus. Lesson: God can turn the hardest times into a harvest, like a seed in the ground. His feast is on 17 March.
2027-03-14.special: Fifth Sunday of Lent. Third Scrutiny of the elect; the Year A readings (the raising of Lazarus) may be used where there are catechumens. Crosses and images may be veiled from today where the bishops' conference permits.
term: Veiling of crosses

A custom kept in many places from the Fifth Sunday of Lent: crosses and images are covered with plain violet cloth. Crosses stay veiled until the Good Friday liturgy, images until the Easter Vigil. It is a fast of the eyes that helps us long to see the Lord.

family.explain: Jesus showed his friends a seed of wheat. If you keep it in your hand, it stays one little seed. But if you plant it in the ground, it seems to die, and then it grows into a plant with many new seeds! Jesus was talking about himself: he would die on the cross and rise again, and bring new life to the whole world.
family.intention: We pray for those who will be baptized at Easter, and for anyone in our family who is struggling.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us give up this week, like a seed, so that love can grow?”

illus: An illustration

A paddy farmer near Kuttanad was asked by his grandson why he threw the best seed rice into the mud every season instead of eating it. The old man laughed and said: if I eat it, it feeds me for one day. If I bury it, it feeds the whole house for a year. Then he added, more quietly: that is what Jesus did with himself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, grain of wheat that fell into the earth, write your covenant on our hearts and draw us to yourself. Amen.
share: I will write it on their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33). What does God want to write on my heart this Lent?
Sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). Who is waiting to see Jesus through me?
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies (John 12:24). What must die in me for Christ to bear fruit?
pm.resp: Create a clean heart in me, O God.
interc: For the elect at their Third Scrutiny, that Christ may call them out of every tomb.
For the Church, that all who seek may see Jesus in her life and worship.
For the persecuted, whose suffering is a grain of wheat for the Church.
For the sick and the dying, that they may share the hope of the resurrection.
For our group, that we may enter Holy Week with clean and willing hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up to draw all people to himself. Make our lives a harvest of his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus enters Jerusalem as a humble King on a colt, greeted with Hosanna.
The Servant does not turn back; Christ empties himself and is obedient to death on a cross.
In Mark's Passion, Jesus dies forsaken, and a Roman centurion confesses him as God's Son.
2027-03-21.action: Take your blessed palm home, place it behind the crucifix, and plan to keep the whole Triduum.
2027-03-21.question: Will my Hosanna today last until Good Friday, or will I run away like the disciples?
catechism: Who is responsible for the death of Christ.
kidsaint: St Turibius of Mogrovejo

A bishop in Peru, far away in South America, more than four hundred years ago. He travelled over mountains and through jungles, often on foot, to meet every family in his huge diocese, and he learned their languages to tell them about Jesus. Lesson: Jesus came to us; we can go to others to bring him.
2027-03-21.special: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord. Blessing of branches and procession; the Passion according to Mark; Holy Week begins.
term: Holy Week

The week from Palm Sunday to Easter, the most sacred of the year. Its heart is the Paschal Triduum: from the Evening Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday, through Good Friday and Holy Saturday, to Evening Prayer on Easter Sunday.

family.explain: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey. People put their coats and green branches on the road and shouted: Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! They welcomed Jesus like a king. But Jesus was a gentle King who came to give his life for us on the cross.
family.intention: We pray that our family may walk with Jesus all through Holy Week.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do this week to stay close to Jesus: go to church, give up something, help someone?”

illus: An illustration

In a coastal parish near Thiruvananthapuram, an old fisherman weaves palm crosses every year for the whole church. A boy once asked why he works so hard on something that will dry up in a week. He held up a finished cross and said: the people waved branches on Sunday and shouted Crucify on Friday. I weave slowly so that I remember, every year, which crowd I want to be in.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, humble King, we welcome you with Hosanna. Give us grace to follow you to the cross. Amen.
share: Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! (Mark 11:9). How do I welcome Jesus into my life?
Not what I want, but what you want (Mark 14:36). Where do I need to pray this prayer?
Truly this man was God's Son! (Mark 15:39). What does the cross reveal to me about Jesus?
pm.resp: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may celebrate Holy Week with faith and devotion.
For all who suffer, feel abandoned or are close to despair, that they may find Christ beside them.
For the persecuted and all who carry the cross, like Simon of Cyrene.
For the elect, who will be baptized at the Easter Vigil.
For our group, that we may stay awake with Jesus and not run away.
pm.close: Father, your Son humbled himself even to death on a cross. Give us a share in his Passion and in his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus, our Passover Lamb, gives his Body and Blood in the Eucharist.
With the words Do this, he gives the Church the priesthood.
He washes the feet of his disciples and commands us to love as he loves.
2027-03-25.action: Stay to adore the Blessed Sacrament at the place of repose tonight, and do one humble act of service at home.
2027-03-25.question: Do I let Jesus wash my feet, and do I wash the feet of others?
catechism: The Eucharist instituted at the Last Supper.
The Mass makes present the sacrifice of the cross.
The apostles made priests of the New Covenant.
kidsaint: St Tarcisius

A boy in Rome long ago, when Christians were persecuted. He was carrying Holy Communion to Christians in prison when some boys stopped him and wanted to see what he was holding. He held Jesus tight to his heart and would not let go, even when they beat him. He died protecting Jesus in the Eucharist. Lesson: Jesus in Holy Communion is our greatest treasure.
2027-03-25.special: Holy Thursday: Chrism Mass (morning or another day); Evening Mass of the Lord's Supper; beginning of the Paschal Triduum. The Annunciation is transferred to Monday 5 April 2027.
term: Mandatum

Latin for “commandment”, from the first words of an antiphon sung at the washing of feet: “A new commandment I give you” (John 13:34). It gives its name to the washing of feet and, in English, to Maundy Thursday.

family.explain: Tonight Jesus had his last supper with his friends. He took bread and said: this is my body. He took the cup and said: this is my blood. That is how he gave us the Holy Mass. Then he knelt down like a servant and washed their feet. At church tonight you will see: the bells ringing loudly at the Gloria and then going quiet until Easter; the priest washing the feet of some people; and at the end a procession taking Jesus in the Eucharist to a beautiful altar full of flowers and candles, where we stay and pray with him. Then the main altar is made bare, and we go home quietly.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, and for all who receive Holy Communion tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “Whose feet can each of us wash this week, by helping them in a humble way?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital in Thiruvananthapuram, on Holy Thursday evening, a chaplain went from bed to bed with a basin and towel and washed the feet of patients who could not go to church: an old fisherman, a young mother after surgery, a boy with a broken leg. A nurse who was not a Christian asked him why. He said: tonight our Lord did this for his friends and told us to do the same. Later she said she had never seen religion look so much like love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this holy night you gave us your Body and Blood and washed the feet of your disciples. Make us one at your table and servants of one another. Amen.
share: This day shall be a day of remembrance for you (Exodus 12:14). What does the Mass make present for me?
This is my body that is for you (1 Corinthians 11:24). How do I prepare for Holy Communion, and how do I give thanks?
You also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14). Whose feet is Jesus asking me to wash?
pm.resp: Our blessing-cup is a communion with the Blood of Christ.
interc: For the Pope, our bishop and all priests, on the day of the priesthood.
For all who will be baptised and confirmed with the holy oils blessed today.
For the sick who will be anointed with the oil of the sick this year.
For all who are betrayed or abandoned by friends.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, keepers of the Passover.
For our group, that we may watch one hour with the Lord tonight.
pm.close: Father, your Son loved his own to the end. Fill us with that love, and make us bread broken for others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Suffering Servant was wounded for our sins; by his bruises we are healed.
In John's Passion Jesus goes freely to the Cross as King and dies saying: It is finished.
We adore the Cross, the throne of grace, and receive Communion; there is no Mass today.
2027-03-26.action: Keep the fast and abstinence, and at three o'clock stop for five minutes of silence before a crucifix.
2027-03-26.question: What does it mean for me that he was wounded for my transgressions?
catechism: Who is responsible for the death of Jesus: all sinners.
The death of Christ is the unique and definitive sacrifice.
The love of Christ “to the end” gives his sacrifice its value.
kidsaint: The Good Thief (St Dismas, by tradition)

Jesus was crucified between two thieves. One of them said: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. Jesus promised him: today you will be with me in Paradise. Lesson: it is never too late to say sorry to Jesus.
2027-03-26.special: Good Friday of the Passion of the Lord: no Mass; Celebration of the Lord's Passion; fasting and abstinence; Collection for the Holy Land.
term: Adoration (Veneration) of the Cross

The central rite of Good Friday: the Cross is shown with the chant “Behold the wood of the Cross,” and each person comes forward to genuflect before it or kiss it. We do not worship wood; we adore Christ who saved us on it.

family.explain: Jesus was dying on the cross, and his mother Mary stood near him with John. Even then Jesus thought of others: he gave Mary to John as his mother, and John to Mary as her son. Then he said: It is finished. He had loved us all the way to the end.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who suffers today, and for all who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family do today to remember how much Jesus loves us?” (For example: silence at three o'clock, a simple meal, the Way of the Cross.)

illus: An illustration

In a Latin parish near Kollam, an old fisherman always came early on Good Friday and stood near the back. When the line formed to kiss the Cross, he waited until everyone else had gone. Asked why, he said: the sea has taken many things from me, and I have said hard words to God because of it. I come last so that I can stay longer at his feet and tell him I am sorry. Then I go home lighter.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we adore you and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
share: He was wounded for our transgressions (Isaiah 53:5). Which of my sins do I see in his wounds?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). Do I take Mary into my home as the beloved disciple did?
Let us approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:16). What do I need to bring to the Cross today?
pm.resp: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.
interc: For the holy Church, that God may keep her in peace and unity.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may continue to grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For all Christians, that we may be gathered into one at the foot of the Cross.
For the sick, the dying, prisoners and refugees, that they may find strength in the crucified Lord.
For our group, that we may never be ashamed of the Cross of Christ.
pm.close: Father, you did not spare your own Son but gave him up for us all. Through his Cross bring us to the glory of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Holy Saturday: Christ lies in the tomb and descends among the dead; the Church waits in silence.
The Vigil has four parts: light, word, water and Eucharist.
At the empty tomb the women hear: He has been raised; go, tell his disciples and Peter.
2027-03-27.action: Bring your family to the Easter Vigil and renew your baptismal promises with a lit candle.
2027-03-27.question: Which darkness in my life do I want the light of the risen Christ to fill tonight?
catechism: Baptism foreshadowed in the Old Testament.
The renewal of baptismal promises at the Easter Vigil.
kidsaint: St Joseph of Arimathea

A rich man who was a secret disciple of Jesus. When Jesus died, he bravely asked Pilate for his body and laid it in his own new tomb in a garden. Lesson: be brave to show your love for Jesus, even when others are afraid.
2027-03-27.special: Holy Saturday: no Mass during the day. The Easter Vigil after nightfall: Service of Light, Liturgy of the Word, Baptismal Liturgy, Liturgy of the Eucharist.
term: Exsultet

The Easter Proclamation, sung by the deacon (or priest or cantor) beside the paschal candle at the beginning of the Vigil. Its name is its first word in Latin: “Exult!” It praises Christ, the true Lamb, and calls this night the night of salvation.

family.explain: Very early on Sunday morning, three women went to the tomb to anoint the body of Jesus. They were worried: who will roll away the big stone? But the stone was already rolled away, and an angel said: Do not be afraid! Jesus is not here. He has risen! Go and tell his friends, and tell Peter too.
family.intention: We pray for the people who will be baptized tonight all over the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What will we bring to the Vigil tonight? Who will hold the candle?” Light a candle at home and say together: Jesus, you are our light.

illus: An illustration

A young woman in Thiruvananthapuram was baptized at the Easter Vigil after two years of preparation. Her grandmother, a Hindu, came with a little brass lamp from home and held it during the Service of Light. Afterwards she said to the parish priest: at home we light the lamp at dusk so that darkness does not rule the house. Tonight I understood what my granddaughter has found: a light that no night can put out.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, we watch with you in the night. Shine in our darkness and raise us with you. Amen.
share: The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5). Where do I need his light most?
We have been buried with him by baptism (Romans 6:4). What must die in me so that I may rise with him?
Go, tell his disciples and Peter (Mark 16:7). Who needs to hear from me that they are forgiven and wanted?
pm.resp: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
interc: For the newly baptized throughout the world, that they may walk in newness of life.
For all who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, that the risen Christ may come to them.
For the dead who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith.
For families who will gather tonight, that Christ may be the light of their homes.
For our group, that we may keep the promises of our Baptism.
pm.close: Father, on this holy night you raised your Son from the dead. Raise us too to newness of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: God raised Jesus on the third day, and we ate and drank with him.
Raised with Christ in Baptism, we seek the things that are above.
At the empty tomb the beloved disciple saw and believed.
2027-03-28.action: Greet everyone today with “Christ is risen!” and bring Easter joy to someone who is alone.
2027-03-28.question: In what part of my life do I still live as if Christ had not risen?
catechism: The Resurrection as a real, historical event.
The Resurrection, source of our own future resurrection.
kidsaint: St Mary Magdalene

Mary loved Jesus very much because he had set her free. She went to his tomb very early on Easter morning, and she was the first to meet him risen and to tell the apostles. Lesson: those who love Jesus run to tell others the good news.
2027-03-28.special: Easter Sunday of the Resurrection of the Lord: the Solemnity of solemnities. Easter Sequence; renewal of baptismal promises; Regina Caeli until Pentecost.
term: Sequence
A poetic hymn sung before the Gospel acclamation on a few great days. The Easter Sequence, Victimae paschali laudes, is obligatory on Easter Sunday and may be sung through the Octave.

family.explain: Very early on Easter morning Mary Magdalene found Jesus' tomb open and empty. Peter and John ran to see. John got there first. They saw the cloths folded neatly. John saw and believed: Jesus is alive! He had beaten death.
family.intention: We thank God for the gift of new life in Jesus, and we pray for those who are sad today.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family show today that we are happy Jesus is alive?” (For example: a special meal, a visit, a phone call to grandparents, singing Alleluia together.)

illus: An illustration

In a fishing village on the Kerala coast, a widow lost her husband to the sea in the months before Lent. On Easter morning, after Mass, she went to the cemetery with her small son. He asked: why are you not crying today? She said: because today Jesus showed us that graves are not the end. One day your father will rise too. Then she lit a candle from the Easter candle on the grave, and they sang Alleluia together, softly.

pm.open: Risen Lord Jesus, you have conquered death. Fill us with your Easter joy and make us your witnesses. Alleluia. Amen.
share: We ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead (Acts 10:41). How do I meet the risen Lord at the table of the Eucharist?
Seek the things that are above (Colossians 3:1). What do I spend most of my time seeking?
He saw and believed (John 20:8). What signs of the risen Lord have I seen in my life?
pm.resp: This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may proclaim the Resurrection with joy.
For the newly baptized, that they may walk always in the light of Christ.
For all who mourn, that the risen Lord may give them hope.
For those who doubt, that they may encounter the living Christ.
For our group, that we may be witnesses of the Resurrection in our homes and at work.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead. Raise us with him and make our lives an Alleluia. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Naaman, a proud army commander, was healed of leprosy by washing seven times in the Jordan.
A little captive girl and his own servants led him to healing.
Jesus was rejected at Nazareth, but God's mercy reaches out to all.
2027-03-01.action: Renew your baptismal promises today, slowly, with holy water.
2027-03-01.question: What simple means of grace do I look down on, waiting for something more impressive?

family.explain: Naaman was a great general, but he had a skin disease. A little servant girl told him about God's prophet. The prophet said: go and wash seven times in the river Jordan. Naaman got angry because it seemed too simple! But when he obeyed, his skin became like a baby's skin, and he believed in God.
family.intention: We pray for those who will be baptized this Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “When was the day of my baptism? Let us find the date and thank God for it.”

illus: An illustration

A retired bank manager in Thrissur had not been to confession in thirty years. He told his granddaughter he would go only if the bishop himself heard him. She laughed and said, Appachan, our parish priest is a priest of the same Jesus. He went, grumbling, on a Lenten Saturday. Afterwards he sat in the car for a long time and said only: so simple. Why did I wait so long?

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went down into the Jordan for us. Wash us, heal us, and make our hearts new. Amen.
share: Go, wash in the Jordan seven times (2 Kings 5:10). Where does God ask me to obey in a simple way?
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God (Psalm 42:2). What is my soul really thirsting for this Lent?
No prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown (Luke 4:24). Whom do I fail to listen to because I know them too well?
pm.resp: My soul is thirsting for the living God.
interc: For the catechumens preparing for Baptism, that their hearts may be made new like Naaman's.
For the sick, especially those with diseases that make others keep away from them.
For migrants and captives, like the little girl from Israel, that they may be treated with dignity.
For those too proud to ask for help or forgiveness.
For our group, that we may find God in simple things.
pm.close: Father, you heal the proud in the humble waters of grace. Bring us all to the font and the altar at Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In the furnace, Azariah offered God a contrite heart and a humble spirit.
Jesus told Peter to forgive not seven times but seventy-seven times.
The servant forgiven a huge debt refused to forgive a small one.
2027-03-02.action: Forgive one person from your heart today, and pray for their good.
2027-03-02.question: Whom am I still holding by the throat, demanding that they pay what they owe me?

family.explain: Peter asked Jesus: how many times must I forgive my brother? Seven times? Jesus said: not seven times, but seventy-seven times! That means: always. God forgives us every time we say sorry, so we must forgive others too.
family.intention: We pray for families where people are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family we need to forgive, or say sorry to, today?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kollam a widow's only son was killed in a road accident by a young driver who had been drinking. At the trial she asked to speak. She told the judge she wanted justice, but not revenge, and that she was praying for the young man every day. Later she visited him in prison. He told the chaplain: I can bear the sentence. What I cannot bear, and what is changing me, is her mercy.

pm.open: Merciful Father, you forgive us more than we can ever repay. Give us hearts that forgive from within. Amen.
share: Yet with a contrite heart and a humble spirit may we be accepted (Daniel 3:39). What can I offer God when I feel I have nothing?
Lord, if another member of the church sins against me, how often should I forgive? (Matthew 18:21). Am I counting?
Should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you? (Matthew 18:33). What mercy have I received that I am not passing on?
pm.resp: Remember your mercies, O Lord.
interc: For all who have been deeply wounded, that God may heal their memories and give them strength to forgive.
For families and communities divided by old quarrels over land, money or words.
For prisoners, and for victims of crime and their families.
For persecuted believers who, like the young men in the furnace, stay faithful under pressure.
For our group, that we may forgive one another from the heart.
pm.close: Father, you cancelled the debt we could never pay. Make us merciful as you are merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses taught Israel that God's law is for life, and that no nation has a God so near.
Jesus came not to abolish the law but to fulfil it.
Those who do and teach the commandments will be called great in the kingdom.
2027-03-03.action: Teach one child one commandment today, with a story from your own life.
2027-03-03.question: Do I see God's commandments as a burden, or as the words of a God who is near?

family.explain: Moses told the people: no one has a God as close as ours! He gave us good laws to help us live well. Do not forget what God has done, and tell your children and grandchildren. Jesus came to help us keep God's law with love.
family.intention: We pray for parents, grandparents and catechists who teach the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of the Ten Commandments do we find hardest at home, and how can we help each other keep it?”

illus: An illustration

In a family in Changanassery the grandmother had a habit: every evening after the rosary she told the children one short story about a commandment. Lying, stealing, honouring parents, keeping Sunday holy. The children laughed at her old-fashioned examples. Twenty years later, a granddaughter working abroad was asked by her manager to sign a false report. She said: I could hear Ammachi's voice telling me the story of the boy and the false weighing scale. She refused, and kept her job anyway.

pm.open: Lord, you are near whenever we call on you. Write your law on our hearts and help us to live it with joy. Amen.
share: For what other great nation has a god so near to it…? (Deuteronomy 4:7). When have I felt God near to me?
Make them known to your children and your children's children (Deuteronomy 4:9). How am I handing on the faith?
I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). Which commandment does Jesus want to bring to its full meaning in me?
pm.resp: Praise the Lord, Jerusalem.
interc: For parents and grandparents, that they may hand on the faith by word and example.
For catechists and teachers of religion.
For lawmakers, that the laws of nations may respect the law of God written in human hearts.
For young people who find God's commandments hard to understand.
For our group, that we may do what we teach.
pm.close: Father, your word runs swiftly and your law gives life. Make us doers of your word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jeremiah lamented a people who would not listen to God's voice.
Jesus cast out demons by the finger of God: the kingdom has come.
St Casimir, a young prince, chose Christ and the poor over the glory of court.
2027-03-04.action: Spend ten minutes in silence with the Gospel today, asking God to speak.
2027-03-04.question: Where has my heart become hard to God's voice because I have heard it so often?
kidsaint: St Casimir

A prince in Poland long ago. He lived in a palace, but he did not care for fine clothes or parties. He loved to pray, he gave to the poor, and he loved Mother Mary very much. He died young, at twenty-five. Lesson: you can love Jesus most, wherever you live.

family.explain: Jesus healed a man who could not speak. Some people said: he did it with the devil's power! But Jesus said: I do it with the power of God. When Jesus is here, God's kingdom is here, and the bad things must go away.
family.intention: We pray for people who are trapped by bad habits, that Jesus may set them free.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way our family can listen to God's voice together this week?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Kannur kept an old alarm clock on her desk that rang every morning at six. For years she pressed it off and went back to sleep, until one day she found she no longer heard it at all. She told her Lenten prayer group: that clock is like my conscience. I had heard God's call to pray so many times that I stopped hearing it. So she moved the clock across the room. This Lent she gets up, walks over, and prays.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, stronger than every evil, open our ears and soften our hearts to hear your voice today. Amen.
share: Obey my voice, and I will be your God (Jeremiah 7:23). Where am I not listening?
O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). What makes my heart hard?
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters (Luke 11:23). Am I gathering or scattering?
pm.resp: If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
interc: For all who preach God's word, that people may hear and not harden their hearts.
For those bound by addiction, fear or occult practices, that Christ may set them free.
For young people in places of wealth and power, that like St Casimir they may choose Christ.
For the people of Lithuania and Poland, through the prayers of St Casimir.
For our group, that we may gather with Christ and not scatter.
pm.close: Father, by the finger of your Spirit you set captives free. Make us gather with your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Through Hosea, God teaches Israel the words to return and promises to love them freely.
Jesus names the first commandment: love God with all your heart; and the second: love your neighbour.
The scribe was not far from the kingdom of God.
2027-03-05.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today, or spend five minutes before a crucifix.
2027-03-05.question: Which part of me, heart, soul, mind or strength, am I still keeping back from God?

family.explain: A man asked Jesus: which is the most important rule? Jesus said: love God with all your heart, and love your neighbour as yourself. These two go together. When we love God, we love the people around us too.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel far from God, that they may come back to his love.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us show love to God and to one person at home today?”

illus: An illustration

A rubber tapper near Pala used to go out before dawn every day. His little son once asked why he stopped at the wayside cross each morning before work. He said: to tell God he comes first. Then why do you also stop at old Mariamma's house? the boy asked. Because, his father said, the One on that cross told me she comes second, right after him, and before me.

pm.open: Lord, our one God, we return to you with words of sorrow. Heal us and make us love you with all our heart. Amen.
share: Take words with you and return to the LORD (Hosea 14:2). What words do I need to bring to God today?
I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily (Hosea 14:5). Where do I need God's dew in my life?
You are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). What still keeps me from going in?
pm.resp: I am the Lord your God: hear my voice.
interc: For all who have drifted from God, that they may hear his invitation to return.
For the Jewish people, our elder brothers and sisters in faith, who pray the Shema each day.
For those who trust in money, power or weapons, that they may find their security in God.
For the lonely and neglected neighbours around us.
For our group, that we may love God with our whole selves and our neighbour as ourselves.
pm.close: Father, you love us freely and heal our unfaithfulness. Make us bloom in your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hosea warns that our love can vanish like morning dew; God desires steadfast love, not sacrifice.
The Pharisee prayed about himself and despised others.
The tax collector prayed, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” and went home justified.
2027-03-06.action: Go to confession today or this weekend, and pray the tax collector's prayer often.
2027-03-06.question: In my prayer and my Lenten practices, am I seeking God's mercy or my own admiration?

family.explain: Two men went to God's house to pray. One said: God, I am better than everyone else! The other said: God, I am a sinner, please be kind to me. Jesus said the second man was the one God was happy with, because he was humble and honest.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to say sorry.
family.ask: Ask: “Can each of us say the humble man's prayer together tonight before bed?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Ernakulam the church committee had two very different members. One kept careful accounts of everything he gave and mentioned it at every meeting. The other, a fisherman who had once been in jail, always sat at the back and said little. When the old parish priest was dying, he asked for the fisherman to come and pray with him. Asked why, he whispered: because he prays like the tax collector. When he asks for mercy, heaven listens.

pm.open: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Amen.
share: Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early (Hosea 6:4). Where has my repentance faded?
For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6). What does God really want from me this Lent?
God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13). Can I pray this without adding any excuses?
pm.resp: It is mercy I desire, and not sacrifice.
interc: For all who will go to confession this weekend, that they may experience God's mercy.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be faces of the Father's mercy.
For those who despise others, that God may give them humble hearts.
For those who think they are too sinful to pray, that they may find courage in the tax collector.
For our group, that our Lenten practices may be humble and hidden.
pm.close: Father, you raise up the humble and receive the contrite. Make our love steadfast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God promises new heavens and a new earth, a world without weeping.
A father believes Jesus' word and his son lives.
St John of God served the sick poor as Christ himself.
2027-03-08.action: Visit, phone or pray with one sick person today.
2027-03-08.question: Do I believe Jesus' word even when I see no sign yet?

family.explain: A father's little boy was very ill. He asked Jesus to come. Jesus said: go home, your son will live. The father believed and walked home, and on the way he heard that his son was well. We can trust what Jesus says.
family.intention: We pray for sick children and their parents.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we know who is sick, and how can we help them this week?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse in a district hospital near Thrissur kept a small card in her pocket through thirty years of night duty. On it she had written: Every bed has Christ in it. When she retired, the younger nurses found the card worn soft at the edges. One of them said: we thought she was just kind; now we know whom she was looking at.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word gives life even from afar. Speak your word over us and over those we love. Amen.
share: I am about to create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17). Where do I long for God to make something new?
The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him (John 4:50). When have I had to trust without seeing?
I was sick and you took care of me (Matthew 25:36). Whom is Christ asking me to care for?
pm.resp: I will praise you, Lord, for you have rescued me.
interc: For sick children and their families, that they may know God's healing and peace.
For doctors, nurses and all who work in hospitals, through the prayers of St John of God.
For those whose faith is waiting for a sign, that they may trust Christ's word.
For the dying, that joy may come to them with the morning of the resurrection.
For our group, that we may carry Christ's word into the week.
pm.close: Father, you turn mourning into dancing. Make us believers in your Son's word and servants of the sick. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel sees a river flowing from the Temple that brings life wherever it goes.
Jesus heals a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years and had no one to help him.
St Frances of Rome served God in her family and in the poor.
2027-03-09.action: Help one person today who has no one to help them.
2027-03-09.question: Do I really want to be made well, or have I grown used to my mat?

family.explain: A man had been sick for thirty-eight years. He had no friend to help him into the healing pool. Jesus asked him: do you want to get well? Then he said: stand up and walk! And the man walked. Jesus wants to heal us too, and he wants us to help people who are alone.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick for a long time, and for those who are lonely.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family, school or street has no one? What can we do for them?”

illus: An illustration

In a coastal parish near Kollam, an elderly fisherman who could no longer walk sat for years at his window watching people go to Sunday Mass. One Lent a group of teenagers decided to take turns pushing his wheelchair to church. On the first Sunday he wept at the door. He said: for eleven years I had no one; today I have six grandsons I never knew I had.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, river of life, you see us lying by the water and ask if we want to be made well. Heal us and make us helpers of others. Amen.
share: Everything will live where the river goes (Ezekiel 47:9). Where does my life need the river of God?
Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool (John 5:7). Who around me has no one?
Do not sin any more (John 5:14). What healing of the soul do I need this Lent?
pm.resp: The Lord of hosts is with us; our stronghold is the God of Jacob.
interc: For the elect preparing for Baptism at Easter, that the living water may make them new.
For the chronically ill and those who care for them over many years.
For the lonely and forgotten, that they may find someone who helps.
For wives and mothers, through the prayers of St Frances of Rome.
For our group, that we may be someone's someone this week.
pm.close: Father, the river from your sanctuary heals and gives life. Let it flow through us to those who have no one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God says: even if a mother forgets her child, I will not forget you.
Jesus does the work of the Father: he gives life and judges.
Whoever hears his word and believes has passed from death to life.
2027-03-10.action: Phone or visit someone who may feel forgotten, and tell them they are remembered.
2027-03-10.question: Where do I need to hear that God has not forgotten me?

family.explain: God says: a mother never forgets her baby. But even if she did, I would never forget you! God has written your name on the palms of his hands. Jesus showed us those hands on the cross.
family.intention: We pray for children who feel alone or unloved, and for all mothers.
family.ask: Ask: “When did you feel that someone remembered you? How can we remember someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in an old age home in Kottayam had no visitors for months. Every morning she held out her palm and traced it with her finger. A young sister asked her what she was doing. She smiled and said: I am reading my name. Isaiah says God wrote it here. My sons may forget, but he does not.

pm.open: Father, you never forget us. Let your mother-love touch every heart that feels forgotten. Amen.
share: Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you (Isaiah 49:15). When have I felt forgotten, and how did God remember me?
My Father is still working, and I also am working (John 5:17). Where do I see God at work in my life now?
Anyone who hears my word… has passed from death to life (John 5:24). What word of Jesus has brought me to life?
pm.resp: The Lord is gracious and merciful.
interc: For exiles, refugees and migrants, that they may find a home and a welcome.
For mothers, especially those who struggle to care for their children.
For the elderly and lonely who feel forgotten.
For the elect, that Christ may bring them from death to life at Easter.
For our group, that we may remember those whom others forget.
pm.close: Father, you have inscribed us on the palms of your hands. Keep us in your love and raise us up with Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Israel made a golden calf; Moses interceded and God spared them.
Jesus calls witnesses: John, his works, the Father and the Scriptures.
We read the Scriptures in order to come to Christ and have life.
2027-03-11.action: Pray by name for someone who has wandered from God.
2027-03-11.question: What golden calf is taking God's place in my life?
