family.explain: When God's people made a golden statue and worshipped it, Moses prayed hard for them, and God forgave them. Moses was like a bridge between God and the people. Jesus is our bridge too, and we can pray for others like Moses did.
family.intention: We pray for people who have stopped praying or going to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anything we love more than God? What can we do about it this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Changanassery prayed for her son for twenty-two years after he stopped going to church. Every night, before sleeping, she said his name at the crucifix. When at last he returned to confession, the priest asked what had brought him back. He said: I do not know. Then he paused and said: yes, I know. My mother never stopped standing between me and the door.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you always live to intercede for us. Teach us to stand in the breach for others. Amen.
share: They have cast for themselves an image of a calf (Exodus 32:8). What do I worship in place of God?
But Moses implored the LORD his God (Exodus 32:11). For whom am I being asked to plead?
Yet you refuse to come to me to have life (John 5:40). Do I read Scripture to meet Christ?
pm.resp: Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people.
interc: For those who have turned to idols of money, power or pleasure, that they may return.
For parents praying for children who have left the faith.
For priests, that they may stand before God for their people.
For Christians and Jews, that we may read the Scriptures with reverence and grow in friendship.
For our group, that we may become faithful intercessors.
pm.close: Father, you heard Moses and spared your people. Hear our prayer through Christ, our High Priest. Amen.

quick: The Book of Wisdom foretells the plot against the righteous man who calls God his Father.
Jesus speaks openly in the Temple; no one can seize him before his hour.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
2027-03-12.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today and keep the Friday abstinence.
2027-03-12.question: When goodness becomes inconvenient, do I hide or stand firm?

family.explain: Some people did not like Jesus because he was good and told the truth. They wanted to hurt him. But God was always close to him. When we are sad or hurt, God is close to us too.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or class who is sad or hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “When did someone stand up for what was right? Can we do that too?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer in a government office in Thiruvananthapuram refused to sign a false bill. For months he was mocked at tea breaks and left out of promotions. One Friday his old father found him praying the Stations alone in the parish church. The young man said: I am only walking with someone who was also inconvenient.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, righteous one, you were mocked for being good. Stay near to us when we are brokenhearted. Amen.
share: Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us (Wisdom 2:12). When has doing right made me unpopular?
No one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come (John 7:30). Do I trust my times to the Father?
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted (Psalm 34:18). Whose broken heart can I sit beside?
pm.resp: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith, that God may be near to them.
For whistle-blowers and all who suffer for honesty.
For the brokenhearted, the grieving and the depressed.
For friendship and respect between Christians and Jews.
For our group, that we may walk the Way of the Cross with love.
pm.close: Father, you are near to the brokenhearted. Keep us faithful in the hour of trial, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jeremiah, plotted against, is like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, a figure of Christ.
The Temple police return without arresting Jesus: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
Nicodemus speaks a small word of fairness, and later honours Jesus at his burial.
2027-03-13.action: Speak up today for someone who is being judged unfairly.
2027-03-13.question: Where do I need the courage of Nicodemus?

family.explain: Some soldiers were sent to arrest Jesus. But when they heard him speak, they could not do it. They went back and said: nobody has ever spoken like this man! Jesus' words are so full of truth and love that they change hearts.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated unfairly.
family.ask: Ask: “Which words of Jesus do you love the most?”

illus: An illustration

In a college staff room in Ernakulam, colleagues were mocking a young teacher who had been accused, without evidence, of copying a paper. An older professor, quiet and shy, put down his cup and said only: has anyone asked her? The room went silent. The young teacher later said that sentence saved her career, and her faith in people.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, no one has ever spoken like you. Let your word disarm us and give us courage. Amen.
share: I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter (Jeremiah 11:19). Where do I see Christ the Lamb in those who suffer today?
Never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). Which word of Jesus has disarmed me?
Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). For whom must I speak up?
pm.resp: O Lord, my God, in you I take refuge.
interc: For those plotted against or betrayed by their own people.
For police and soldiers, that they may serve justice and protect the innocent.
For those who are judged without a hearing, that truth may come to light.
For timid believers, that they may grow in courage like Nicodemus.
For our group, that the word of Jesus may change our hearts.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, the Lamb, whose words are spirit and life. Make us his witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Susanna chose to fall into the hands of the wicked rather than sin before the Lord.
God heard her prayer and raised up Daniel to defend her.
Jesus refused to condemn the sinful woman and told her to sin no more.
2027-03-15.action: Put down one judgment today: say nothing critical about anyone until bedtime.
2027-03-15.question: Am I standing in the crowd with a stone, or kneeling before Jesus asking for mercy?

family.explain: Some men brought a woman who had done wrong and wanted to throw stones at her. Jesus said: whoever has never sinned can throw the first stone. Nobody could! They all went away. Jesus forgave her and said: go, and do not sin again.
family.intention: We pray for people who are judged unfairly, and for all who need forgiveness.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family or class we have been unkind to or have judged? How can we make it right?”

illus: An illustration

A story told in a Thrissur parish: a woman was accused in the neighbourhood of stealing from the house where she worked. The gossip spread quickly. Only one old neighbour refused to repeat it, saying: I was not there, and neither were you. A week later the missing money was found where the owner himself had put it away. The women who had talked went to her one by one to say sorry. She told the parish priest later that the old neighbour's silence had been her Daniel.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you did not condemn the sinner, and you defended the innocent. Teach us mercy and give us courage. Amen.
share: I choose not to do it… rather than sin in the sight of the Lord (Daniel 13:23). Where do I need Susanna's courage?
Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone (John 8:7). Whom am I quick to judge?
Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). Which sin do I need to leave behind this Lent?
pm.resp: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I fear no evil; for you are with me.
interc: For those falsely accused, in courts, workplaces and families, that the truth may come to light.
For judges, police and lawyers, that they may be honest and fair.
For women and girls who suffer abuse and threats, that they may be protected and believed.
For all who are ashamed of their sins, that they may meet the mercy of Jesus in confession.
For our group, that we may never use our tongues as stones.
pm.close: Father, you see what is secret and you save those who hope in you. Make us merciful as your Son is merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Israel grew impatient and complained against God and the manna.
God told Moses to lift up a bronze serpent; whoever looked at it lived.
Jesus, lifted up on the cross, reveals that he is I AM and gives life to all who look to him.
2027-03-16.action: Pray today before a crucifix, at home or in church, for five minutes.
2027-03-16.question: What is the poison in my life that I need to bring to the cross of Jesus?

family.explain: On the long walk through the desert God's people grumbled and said they hated the bread God gave them. Snakes bit them and they became sick. God told Moses to put a snake made of bronze on a pole. Whoever looked at it got better! Jesus said: I will be lifted up on the cross like that, so that everyone who looks to me will live.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sick, and for those who have lost hope.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we grumble about at home? Can we say thank you to God for it instead?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse in a Kozhikode hospital kept a small crucifix in her pocket during night duty. A young man brought in after a snakebite was terrified while they waited for the anti-venom to work. She did not preach. She put the crucifix in his hand and said: hold this and breathe. Months later he came back to thank her and said: I did not know the story of Moses then. I only knew that someone had been hurt more than me and was holding on.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up on the cross, we look to you. Heal us and give us life. Amen.
share: The people became impatient on the way (Numbers 21:4). Where am I impatient with God?
Everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). What wound do I need to bring to Jesus?
When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). What does the cross tell me about who Jesus is?
pm.resp: O Lord, listen to my prayer and let my cry for help reach you.
interc: For all who are seriously ill, especially victims of snakebite and accidents, and for those who care for them.
For those tired of the journey of faith, that they may not give up.
For those who complain and are bitter, that they may learn gratitude.
For all who will be baptized at Easter, that they may look to Christ and live.
For our group, that we may stay close to the cross this Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, you lifted up your Son on the cross to be our healing. Draw all people to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Three young men refused to worship the golden statue, even if God did not rescue them.
God was with them in the fire, and they came out unharmed.
Jesus frees us from slavery to sin; St Patrick, once a slave, became the apostle of Ireland.
2027-03-17.action: Say St Patrick's prayer today: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me.
2027-03-17.question: Would I stay faithful to God even if he did not give me what I am asking for?

family.explain: A king ordered everyone to bow down to a big golden statue. Three young men said: we will only worship God. They were thrown into a fire, but God was with them and they were not even burnt! Jesus also says: if I make you free, you will be really free.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are punished for their faith, and for the people of Ireland on St Patrick's day.
family.ask: Ask: “What are the golden statues today that people bow to instead of God?”

illus: An illustration

St Patrick tells in his Confession how, as a teenage slave herding sheep in Ireland, he prayed a hundred times a day and almost as many times at night, in snow and frost and rain. Years later, when he could have stayed safe at home in Britain, he dreamed he heard the Irish calling him: come and walk among us again. He went back to the people who had enslaved him, this time free, and brought them Christ.

pm.open: Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our ancestors. Walk with us in the fire and make us free. Amen.
share: But if not… we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:18). Is my faith a bargain or a gift of myself?
I see four men unbound, walking in the middle of the fire (Daniel 3:92). Where have I felt God with me in a fire?
If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:36). From what slavery do I need to be freed?
pm.resp: To you glory and praise for evermore.
interc: For Christians who suffer for refusing to deny their faith.
For all who are trapped in addiction or slavery of any kind, that the Son may set them free.
For the Church in Ireland and for Irish missionaries in India and across the world, through the prayers of St Patrick.
For victims of human trafficking, that they may be rescued and healed.
For our group, that we may continue in the word of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son makes us free indeed. Keep us faithful in every trial. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God made an everlasting covenant with Abraham and gave him a new name.
Jesus says that Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and that before Abraham was, I AM.
St Cyril of Jerusalem taught the catechumens and defended the divinity of Christ.
2027-03-18.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-03-18.question: Do I believe, with all my heart, that Jesus is God, the I AM before Abraham?

family.explain: God made a special promise to Abram: you will be the father of many nations! And God gave him a new name, Abraham. God promised to be his God and the God of his children for ever. Jesus said: before Abraham was born, I AM. Jesus is God, who was there before everything.
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we baptized? Shall we look for the date and celebrate it this year?”

illus: An illustration

In a village parish near Kollam the catechism teacher had the children bring their baptism certificates to class. One girl discovered she had been baptized on the same date as her grandmother, sixty years apart. The old woman cried when she heard it and said: God has kept his promise for three generations in our family. The class wrote the dates on a chart and promised to pray for each other on their baptism days.

pm.open: God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, you remember your covenant for ever. Lord Jesus, before Abraham was, you are. We adore you. Amen.
share: No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham (Genesis 17:5). What new name, what mission, has God given me?
Whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). How do I keep the word of Jesus?
Before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). Do I worship Jesus as God?
pm.resp: The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
interc: For the elect and catechumens preparing for Easter Baptism, through the prayers of St Cyril.
For catechists and teachers of the faith, that they may teach with clarity and love.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and faithfulness to his covenant.
For Christians in Jerusalem and the Holy Land, especially as Holy Week approaches.
For our group, that we may live our baptismal promises.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to your covenant for a thousand generations. Make us faithful children of Abraham in Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's promise to David was fulfilled through Joseph, who gave Jesus his name and his place in David's line.
Joseph, a righteous man, believed the angel and took Mary as his wife.
St Joseph is Patron of the Universal Church, of families, workers and a happy death.
2027-03-19.action: Do at once one thing you know God is asking of you, as Joseph did.
2027-03-19.question: When God's plan upsets mine, do I respond like Joseph, with trust and action?
catechism: The angel announces to Joseph the birth of the Messiah.
The hidden life of Jesus at Nazareth with Mary and Joseph.
St Joseph, patron of a happy death.
kidsaint: St Joseph

Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth. God asked him to look after Mary and baby Jesus. He listened to God's angel in his dreams and always obeyed straight away. He kept Jesus safe, taught him to work and loved him like the best of fathers. Lesson: listen to God and do what he asks, quickly and with love.
2027-03-19.special: Solemnity of St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary. White vestments, Gloria and Creed; Friday abstinence does not bind on this solemnity.
term: Solemnity

The highest rank of celebration in the Roman calendar. A solemnity has the Gloria and the Creed and its own readings, and when it falls on a Friday the obligation of abstinence does not apply (can. 1251).

family.explain: Joseph was going to marry Mary. When he learned she was going to have a baby, he was worried. But an angel told him in a dream: do not be afraid, the baby is from the Holy Spirit, call him Jesus. Joseph woke up and did just what the angel said. He became the protector of Jesus and Mary.
family.intention: We pray for all fathers, for workers who have no work, and for the dying.
family.ask: Ask: “How does our father, or someone like a father to us, protect and care for our family? Let us thank him today.”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kottayam, the St Joseph's day meal draws hundreds: day labourers, old people living alone, children, migrant workers who speak little Malayalam. A retired carpenter has served rice there for forty years. Asked why, he said: St Joseph fed Jesus with the work of his hands. I am only a carpenter too. Once a year I can feed Jesus in these people.

pm.open: St Joseph, son of David and guardian of the Redeemer, pray for us, and teach us to listen and obey. Amen.
share: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid (Matthew 1:20). What fear keeps me from doing God's will?
He did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). How quickly do I obey when God speaks?
Hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Where do I need hope against hope?
pm.resp: His dynasty shall last for ever.
interc: For the whole Church, entrusted to the protection of St Joseph.
For fathers, that they may be loving, faithful and present like Joseph.
For workers, the unemployed and migrants, that they may find dignified work.
For families facing hard decisions, that they may hear God's voice.
For the dying, that St Joseph may obtain for them a holy death in the arms of Jesus and Mary.
pm.close: Father, you entrusted the beginnings of our salvation to the faithful care of St Joseph. Through his prayers, protect your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel promises that God will make his scattered people one nation with one shepherd.
Caiaphas unknowingly prophesied that Jesus would die to gather God's children into one.
Holy Week begins tomorrow: Jesus comes to the feast to give his life.
2027-03-20.action: Make peace with one person today before Holy Week begins.
2027-03-20.question: Am I a person who gathers people together, or one who scatters?

family.explain: After Jesus raised Lazarus, some leaders were afraid and decided that Jesus must die. The high priest said: it is better for one man to die for the people. Without knowing it, he was saying something true: Jesus would die to bring all God's children together into one family.
family.intention: We pray for families that are divided, and for unity among all Christians.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we are not talking to? How can we make peace before Palm Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in Ernakulam had not spoken for six years after a quarrel over a small piece of land. Their old mother asked only one thing for her birthday, which fell in Holy Week: that both sons would carry palms together in the procession. They came, stiff and silent, and walked side by side. By the time the Passion was read, the younger had put his hand on the older's shoulder. The land is still divided, their mother says, but my sons are not.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you died to gather into one the scattered children of God. Gather us into your one flock. Amen.
share: I will make them one nation… never again shall they be divided (Ezekiel 37:22). Where is there division around me?
It is better for you to have one man die for the people (John 11:50). What does it mean to me that Jesus died for me?
Surely he will not come to the festival, will he? (John 11:56). How will I welcome Jesus this Holy Week?
pm.resp: The Lord will guard us as a shepherd guards his flock.
interc: For Christian unity, that all who believe in Christ may be one.
For divided families, that they may be reconciled this Holy Week.
For the Holy Land and all places torn by conflict, that God may give a covenant of peace.
For the elect who will be baptized at the Easter Vigil.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus closely through Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to gather your scattered children. Make us one in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Servant of the Lord is gentle: he does not break the bruised reed.
Mary anoints the feet of Jesus with costly nard for the day of his burial.
Holy Week asks for love that does not count the cost.
2027-03-22.action: Give Jesus one costly gift of time today: half an hour of prayer before the Blessed Sacrament or with the Gospel of the Passion.
2027-03-22.question: What is my alabaster jar, the precious thing I am keeping back from Jesus?

family.explain: Mary loved Jesus so much that she poured very expensive perfume on his feet. The whole house smelt beautiful. Jesus knew he was going to die soon, and Mary's gift showed him how much she loved him.
family.intention: We pray for all who will celebrate Holy Week, that they may love Jesus more.
family.ask: Ask: “What beautiful gift can each of us give to Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Thrissur kept a small bottle of attar, a gift from her late husband, for thirty years. She never used it. One Holy Week she heard the Gospel of Mary at Bethany and went home thinking. On Holy Thursday she brought the bottle to the parish and asked that it be used to perfume the place of the altar of repose. When people knelt there that night, they said the chapel smelt like a garden. She said only: I was keeping it for a special day, and there is no day more special than this.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were anointed at Bethany for the day of your burial. Receive the love we pour out at your feet this Holy Week. Amen.
share: A bruised reed he will not break (Isaiah 42:3). Where am I a bruised reed, and where do I break others?
Mary took a pound of costly perfume (John 12:3). What costly gift can I give Jesus this week?
He was a thief (John 12:6). Where does money or self-interest rule my heart?
pm.resp: The Lord is my light and my salvation.
interc: For the Church as she enters Holy Week, that she may follow her Lord faithfully.
For those who are broken and discouraged, that the gentle Servant may lift them up.
For the poor, that our love for Jesus may overflow into love for them.
For prisoners and those who sit in darkness.
For our group, that we may keep this week holy.
pm.close: Father, your Servant brings justice and light to the nations. Make us gentle and generous like him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Servant is called from the womb and made a light to the nations.
Judas takes the morsel and goes out: and it was night.
Peter promises to die for Jesus and will deny him, but he will weep and return.
2027-03-23.action: Go to confession this week, before the Triduum begins.
2027-03-23.question: After I fail, do I go out into the night like Judas, or turn back with tears like Peter?

family.explain: Peter said to Jesus: I will die for you! But Jesus knew that Peter would be afraid and would say three times that he did not know him. Later Peter was very sorry and cried, and Jesus forgave him. Jesus always forgives us when we come back.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is sad because of their sins, that they may come back to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to say sorry to today?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a coastal parish near Kollam stopped going to church after a public quarrel and some foolish words he was ashamed of. For three years he avoided the priest. One Holy Week his little sister asked him to take her to the penitential service. He stood at the back. When the priest read “Peter went out and wept bitterly,” he found himself in the confession line. He said later: I thought I was Judas. That night I found out I was allowed to be Peter.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, in the night of betrayal you kept on loving. Look on us as you looked on Peter. Amen.
share: I have labored in vain (Isaiah 49:4). Where do I feel my efforts have come to nothing?
And it was night (John 13:30). Where is there night in my heart?
I will lay down my life for you (John 13:37). Do I trust my own strength more than his grace?
pm.resp: I will sing of your salvation.
interc: For missionaries who carry the light of Christ to the ends of the earth.
For those who have betrayed the trust of others, that they may not despair.
For all who have left the faith, that they may return like Peter.
For priests hearing confessions this Holy Week.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus faithfully this week.
pm.close: Father, you made your Servant a light to the nations. Keep us in his light, and let no one be lost in the night. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Servant listens to God every morning and does not turn back from suffering.
Judas sells Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Each disciple asks, Surely not I, Lord? We ask it too, and trust his mercy.
2027-03-24.action: Prepare your home and heart for the Triduum: confession, family timetable, and the Good Friday fast.
2027-03-24.question: For what price am I tempted to sell my friendship with Jesus?

family.explain: Judas was one of Jesus' friends, but he sold Jesus for thirty silver coins. That was a very sad thing. Jesus still loved him. Jesus is our best friend, and we never want to trade him for anything.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always stay close to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to get our home ready for Holy Thursday, Good Friday and Easter?”

illus: An illustration

A businessman in Kochi was offered a large contract if he would sign false accounts. It was Holy Week. On Wednesday evening he heard the Gospel: “What will you give me if I betray him to you?” He went home and told his wife he could not sign. They lost the contract and had a hard year. Years later he said to his son: the price was very high, but it was much less than thirty pieces of silver. I would have sold my Lord and my peace.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were sold for thirty pieces of silver and you did not turn back. Open our ears morning by morning and keep us faithful. Amen.
share: Morning by morning he wakens my ear (Isaiah 50:4). Do I begin my day by listening to God?
What will you give me if I betray him? (Matthew 26:15). For what do I sell my faith?
Surely not I, Lord? (Matthew 26:22). Do I ask this question humbly, or do I trust myself too much?
pm.resp: Lord, in your great love, answer me.
interc: For all who are tempted to betray a friend, a spouse or their conscience for money.
For those who suffer insult and violence for doing what is right.
For the despairing, that they may find the mercy Judas refused.
For all who prepare the Holy Week liturgies in our parish.
For our group, that we may enter the Triduum with listening hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son set his face like flint to do your will. Help us to follow him faithfully through these holy days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: God raised Jesus up; death could not hold him; we are all witnesses.
The women ran from the tomb with fear and great joy, and met the risen Lord.
The truth of the Resurrection cannot be bought or explained away.
2027-03-29.action: Tell one person today, in your own words, that Christ is risen.
2027-03-29.question: What fear keeps me from speaking about the risen Lord?
catechism: Christ's body did not see corruption.
Sunday and the joy of the Resurrection.
kidsaint: The holy women at the tomb

Some women who loved Jesus went to his tomb on Easter morning. They were the first to hear that he was alive, and Jesus met them on the road. They ran to tell the apostles. Lesson: good news is for sharing!
2027-03-29.special: Monday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal.
term: Octave
From the Latin for “eighth”: an eight-day celebration of a great feast. Today only Easter and Christmas have octaves in the Roman calendar. The Easter Octave ends on the Second Sunday of Easter.

family.explain: The women ran from the tomb, a little scared and very happy. Suddenly Jesus was there! He said hello, and they held his feet and worshipped him. Jesus said: Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers.
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid, that Jesus may give them his peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we tell today that Jesus is alive? How will we tell them?”

illus: An illustration

A teenage boy from a parish in Ernakulam was teased at college for going to Mass on Easter Monday, a holiday. A friend asked him half-mockingly: do you really believe a dead man came back? He answered: I believe because of my grandmother. She buried two children and her husband, and every Easter she still sings louder than anyone. Something real must have happened for that. The friend came with him the next Sunday.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you met the women on the road. Meet us now, and take away our fear. Alleluia. Amen.
share: It was impossible for him to be held in its power (Acts 2:24). What power of death do I fear that Christ has already broken?
They left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy (Matthew 28:8). Do I feel both fear and joy in my faith?
Go and tell my brothers (Matthew 28:10). Which brother or sister is waiting to hear from me?
pm.resp: Keep me safe, O God; you are my hope.
interc: For the newly baptized, that they may hold fast to the faith they have received.
For preachers and catechists, that they may proclaim the Resurrection with boldness.
For those who explain away the faith, that they may meet the living Lord.
For those who live in fear, that they may hear Jesus say: do not be afraid.
For our group, that we may run with the good news to those around us.
pm.close: Father, you freed your Son from death. Free us from fear and make us witnesses of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Cut to the heart, the crowd asked: What should we do? Peter: repent and be baptized.
Mary Magdalene, weeping at the tomb, recognized Jesus when he called her name.
Sent to the disciples, she announced: I have seen the Lord.
2027-03-30.action: Find the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-03-30.question: Do I recognize the Lord's voice when he calls my name?
catechism: Mary Magdalene, first witness of the risen Lord.
Peter's call to Baptism at Pentecost.
kidsaint: St Mary Magdalene

Mary was crying at Jesus' tomb because she thought someone had taken him away. Then someone said her name: Mary! It was Jesus! She was so happy she ran to tell the apostles: I have seen the Lord! Lesson: Jesus knows your name and loves you.
2027-03-30.special: Tuesday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal.
term: Neophyte
From the Greek for “newly planted”: a person newly baptized, especially at the Easter Vigil. Neophytes are accompanied by the community during the Easter season (mystagogy).

family.explain: Mary Magdalene was crying outside Jesus' tomb. She saw a man and thought he was the gardener. But then he said her name: Mary! She knew at once it was Jesus. He sent her to tell his friends, and she said: I have seen the Lord!
family.intention: We pray for the people who were baptized at Easter, that they may always know Jesus' voice.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the story of your name? Who chose it?” Then thank God that he knows each of us by name.

illus: An illustration

A woman in Thrissur lost her husband and stopped going to church; for months she sat at home weeping. On Easter Tuesday the parish priest visited and did not preach. He only said, gently, her baptismal name: Maria. She later said: no one had called me by that name since my mother died. Something in me turned around, like Mary at the tomb. The next Sunday she was back, and later she began visiting widows herself.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you called Mary by name. Call each of us now, and help us to hear your voice. Alleluia. Amen.
share: They were cut to the heart (Acts 2:37). When has God's word pierced my heart?
Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for? (John 20:15). What am I really looking for?
I have seen the Lord (John 20:18). Where have I seen the risen Lord this week?
pm.resp: The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For the newly baptized, that they may grow in the grace they have received.
For those who are weeping, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
For women in the Church, that their witness to the risen Christ may be honoured.
For those far away, that the promise of the Spirit may reach them.
For our group, that we may go out and tell what we have seen.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and sent Mary to announce it. Send us too as witnesses of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter healed the lame man: what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus, walk.
On the road to Emmaus Jesus opened the Scriptures and the disciples' hearts burned.
They recognized him in the breaking of the bread, the Eucharist.
2027-03-31.action: Before supper tonight, pray together: “Stay with us, Lord, because it is almost evening.”
2027-03-31.question: Where in my life am I saying “we had hoped,” and how is Jesus walking with me there?
catechism: The Eucharist called “the breaking of bread.”
Christ opens our minds to understand the Scriptures.
kidsaint: St Cleopas

Cleopas and his friend were walking home very sad because Jesus had died. A stranger walked with them and explained the Bible. At supper he broke bread, and they saw it was Jesus! Lesson: Jesus walks with us when we are sad, and we meet him at Mass.
2027-03-31.special: Wednesday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal.
term: Mystagogy

From the Greek for “leading into the mysteries”: the teaching given especially in the Easter season to help the newly baptized, and all the faithful, understand and live the sacraments. Emmaus is its model: the Lord explains the Scriptures and is known in the breaking of bread.

family.explain: Two friends of Jesus were walking home sad. A man walked with them and explained the Bible so beautifully that their hearts felt warm. They invited him for supper. When he broke the bread, they saw: it was Jesus! Then he disappeared, and they ran all the way back to tell the others.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sad or have lost hope, that Jesus may walk with them.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we meet Jesus in our family?” Before supper, invite him: Stay with us, Lord.

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Kottayam stopped going to Mass after a quarrel with the parish council. Every evening he walked alone along the canal. One Easter week a young assistant priest began walking the same path, without mentioning the Church. They talked about books, then about the Gospels. On the third evening the old man said: you make the Bible burn like it did when I was a boy. Will you say Mass in my house for my wife, who cannot walk? The priest did. The next Sunday the teacher was back in the parish.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, stay with us, for it is almost evening. Open the Scriptures to us and make yourself known to us. Alleluia. Amen.
share: I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you (Acts 3:6). What can I give in Jesus' name today?
We had hoped (Luke 24:21). What hope of mine has died, and how might Jesus be walking beside it?
They recognized him in the breaking of the bread (Luke 24:35). How do I prepare to recognize him at Mass?
pm.resp: Rejoice, O hearts that seek the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may give Christ, not silver or gold, to the poor and the lame.
For those who have lost hope, that the risen Lord may walk with them.
For preachers, that they may open the Scriptures until hearts burn.
For those who have drifted from the Eucharist, that they may return to the breaking of bread.
For our group, that we may recognize Jesus at the altar and run to tell others.
pm.close: Father, your Son walked with the disciples and broke bread with them. Stay with us and make us witnesses of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Church says: Laetare, rejoice! We are halfway through Lent, and the violet is touched with rose, like the sky before dawn. Why rejoice in a season of penance? Because today's readings tell us how much God loves us.

The first reading tells of a people who were exceedingly unfaithful. Yet God sent persistently to them by his messengers, because he had compassion on his people (2 Chronicles 36:15). They mocked his prophets and ended in exile, weeping by the rivers of Babylon. But God did not abandon them. After seventy years he stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, and the word went out: let him go up. God always has a way home for us.

In the Gospel Jesus tells Nicodemus: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). In the desert those bitten by serpents looked at the bronze serpent and lived. We, bitten by sin, look at Jesus on the cross and live.

Then the words we should all know by heart: for God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life (John 3:16). God did not send the Son to condemn the world, but to save it. If there is judgment, it is because we prefer the darkness. Jesus invites us to come to the light.

St Paul says: God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (Ephesians 2:4–5). By grace you have been saved. It is a gift. And we are created in Christ Jesus for good works. Our Lenten works do not buy God's love; they answer it.

So let us rejoice today. Let us look at the cross and live. Let us bring our hidden sins into the light of confession. And let us pray for the elect, who today ask the Lord to open their eyes, so that at Easter they may see. Amen.
kids: Children, today is called Laetare Sunday, rejoice Sunday! Why? Because God loves us so much that he gave us Jesus. Let us learn this verse: God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.
When the people in the desert were bitten by snakes, they looked at the bronze snake and got better. When we are sad or have done wrong, we can look at Jesus on the cross and he makes us better.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today Jeremiah speaks to a people whose covenant with God lay broken. And God says: the days are surely coming… when I will make a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31). Not on stone, but on the heart: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts.

At the Last Supper Jesus took a cup and said: this cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood. At every Mass that covenant is renewed. And God's promise comes true: I will forgive their iniquity, and remember their sin no more.

In the Gospel some Greeks come and say to Philip: sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). That is the longing of every human heart. And Jesus answers: the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

But what kind of glory? Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24). The glory of Jesus is the cross. His soul is troubled, as Hebrews says, with loud cries and tears; yet he says: Father, glorify your name. And from the cross he will draw all people to himself.

Every Christian is called to be a grain of wheat. Whoever serves me must follow me. We die a little each time we forgive, each time we give without being thanked, each time we choose God over ourselves. It feels like loss. It is really a harvest.

Today, in many churches, the crosses are veiled, and in some the Church celebrates the Third Scrutiny with the Gospel of Lazarus. Let us pray for the elect. And let us pray the Psalm with all our heart: create in me a clean heart, O God. Then, at Easter, we will see Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus held up a seed of wheat and said: if this seed is planted in the ground, it can grow into a big plant with lots of new seeds!
Jesus is like that seed. He died on the cross and rose again, and now his life is in all of us. When we share and forgive, we are seeds of love too.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we waved palms and sang Hosanna. And a few minutes later we heard ourselves say: Crucify him! Palm Sunday holds both, the joy of the welcome and the sorrow of the cross, because the King who enters Jerusalem is going there to die.

Jesus comes on a colt, as Zechariah foretold: humble and riding on a donkey. Not a war horse, not an army. The crowd cries: Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! (Mark 11:9). Hosanna means save us. He will save us, but not in the way they expected.

Isaiah shows us the Servant: I gave my back to those who struck me… I did not hide my face from insult and spitting (Isaiah 50:6). And in Gethsemane Jesus prays: Abba, Father… remove this cup from me; yet, not what I want, but what you want (Mark 14:36). He does not turn back. He freely gives himself for us.

On the cross he cries out: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? (Mark 15:34). He enters into every human loneliness and abandonment. Psalm 22, which begins in that cry, ends in praise. And at that moment a Roman soldier, a foreigner, says what the disciples had not been able to say: truly this man was God's Son! (Mark 15:39).

St Paul sums it up: he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him (Philippians 2:8–9). The way down is the way up. The cross is the throne of the King.

Take your palm home and put it behind the crucifix. Let it ask you every day: which crowd am I in? Come back on Thursday evening, on Friday afternoon, and on Saturday night for the Easter Vigil. Walk with Jesus to the end, and you will see the morning of the Resurrection. Amen.
kids: Children, today we carried palms like the people in Jerusalem, and shouted Hosanna for Jesus our King! But Jesus was a gentle King, riding on a little donkey.
This week Jesus will die on the cross for us and rise again at Easter. Keep your palm near a cross at home, and say every night: Jesus, I love you, thank you for dying for me.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight the Church enters the holiest days of the year. Lent is over; the Triduum has begun. And it begins at a table. The first reading takes us to Egypt: take a lamb without blemish, put its blood on the doorposts, eat it in haste with your sandals on. It is the passover of the LORD… when I see the blood, I will pass over you (Exodus 12:11, 13).

Jesus kept that Passover with his disciples. But on that night he became the Lamb. St Paul writes: on the night when he was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, this is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me. And the cup: this cup is the new covenant in my blood (1 Corinthians 11:23–25).

These are not just beautiful words. When the priest says them at the altar, Christ himself acts, and the bread and wine become his true Body and Blood. The sacrifice of the cross is made present among us. That is why we kneel, why we prepare for Communion with a clean heart, and why we stay with him tonight in adoration.

Do this, he said. With those words he gave us priests. Tonight let us thank God for every priest who has baptised us, absolved us and fed us. And let us pray that young men in our parishes may hear his call.

Then St John tells us what the Eucharist means. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end (John 13:1). Jesus rises from the table, ties a towel around himself and washes their feet. Peter protests, but Jesus says: unless I wash you, you have no share with me. And then: if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14).

In a moment the priest will kneel and wash feet, as Jesus did. Then we will carry the Lord to the place of repose, and the altar will be stripped bare. Stay with him tonight. Could you not keep awake with me one hour? And tomorrow, at home and at work, take up the towel. The one who receives the Body given for us must become bread broken for others. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight Jesus gave us a wonderful gift. At his Last Supper he took bread and said: this is my body. Every time we go to Mass, Jesus gives himself to us in Holy Communion!
Then Jesus knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He wants us to help one another too. Tonight, help at home without being asked, and say thank you to Jesus for the Holy Mass.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, look at our church today. The altar is bare. The tabernacle is empty and its door stands open. There are no flowers, no bells, no Mass. Everything is stripped away so that only one thing remains: the Cross. Today we stand where Mary stood, at the foot of the Cross.

Seven hundred years before Christ, Isaiah saw him: he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed (Isaiah 53:5). Like a lamb led to the slaughter, he did not open his mouth. When we look at the crucifix, we must say: that is what my sin cost. And that is how much I am loved.

St John shows us that Jesus is not a helpless victim. In the garden he steps forward: whom are you looking for? I am he. Before Pilate he speaks of the truth. He carries his own cross. Above his head is written: Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews. The Cross is his throne. He reigns by giving his life.

Who killed Jesus? Not a people. The Church teaches that we must never blame the Jewish people for his death. All sinners caused his Passion; I did, you did (Catechism 598). So today we do not point at others. We strike our own breast. And we hear him say from the cross: Father, forgive them.

From the cross he gives us his mother: here is your mother (John 19:27). Then he says: it is finished, bows his head and hands over his spirit (John 19:30). The soldier's spear opens his side, and blood and water flow: the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the heart of Christ.

Soon we will come forward to adore the Cross. As you bend to kiss it, give him your sins, your sorrows and your dead. He is the high priest who sympathizes with our weakness. Let us approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:16). We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today the church is very quiet and the altar is bare, because we remember that Jesus died on the cross for us. He loved us so much that he gave his whole life.
When you kiss the cross today, say in your heart: thank you, Jesus. I love you. I am sorry for my sins.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight we began in darkness. Then a single fire, a single candle, and the cry: the Light of Christ! And from that one flame the whole church was filled with light. That is Easter. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it (John 1:5).

Then we listened to the whole story of God's love: creation, Abraham's faith, the sea opening for Israel, the promise of an everlasting love, of clean water and a new heart. All of it was leading to tonight. As Jesus explained the Scriptures to the disciples on the road, the Church explains them to us: everything speaks of him.

In the Gospel, the women go to the tomb with spices, worried about a stone. They expect to anoint a dead body. Instead they meet a messenger: do not be alarmed; you are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has been raised; he is not here (Mark 16:6). The stones we worry about are already rolled away by God.

And notice the next words: go, tell his disciples and Peter (Mark 16:7). Peter, who denied him three times. The first message of Easter has his name in it. Whatever you have done, the risen Lord names you tonight and calls you back.

In a few moments we will renew the promises of our Baptism. St Paul says: we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:4). We will reject sin and Satan, and say: I do believe. Say it with your whole heart.

Then, for the first time since Thursday, the altar will be set, and the risen Lord will give himself to us in the Eucharist. Christ, raised from the dead, will never die again. Let the Alleluia return to your lips and never leave your life. Christ is risen! He is truly risen! Amen.
kids: Children, tonight the church was dark, and then the big Easter candle was lit and everyone's little candle took light from it. Jesus is our light!
The women went to Jesus' tomb and found it empty. An angel said: he is risen! Let us shout it too: Jesus is risen! Alleluia!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Christ is risen! He is truly risen! Alleluia! This is the day that the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone (Psalm 118:22).

Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb. Perhaps you too have come to Easter in some darkness: a loss, an illness, a sin, a worry. Mary found the stone rolled away. The darkness was already breaking, though she did not yet know it.

Peter and John ran. John looked in and saw the linen wrappings lying there, and the cloth from Jesus' head rolled up by itself. Then he went in, and he saw and believed (John 20:8). He saw an empty tomb, and he believed in a living Lord. That is our faith: we see signs, and we believe in him.

And this faith is not a dream. Peter tells Cornelius: God raised him on the third day and allowed him to appear… to us who were chosen by God as witnesses, and who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead (Acts 10:40–41). The Apostles ate with him, touched him and died for him. The Resurrection is real.

St Paul says: so if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above (Colossians 3:1). At Baptism we were raised with him. So Easter must show in our lives: forgiveness instead of grudges, hope instead of fear, generosity instead of greed.

Today we will renew our baptismal promises, and then receive the risen Lord in the Eucharist. Let us go home as Easter people: greet one another with Christ is risen, visit someone lonely, and let the Alleluia be our song. Because he lives, death is not the end. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is alive! On Easter morning his friends found his tomb empty. He had risen from the dead!
Today let us say to everyone: Jesus is risen! And let us sing Alleluia, which means: praise the Lord!

homily: Dear friends, Naaman had everything: power, wealth, victories, the favour of his king. But he had leprosy. And the first person who points him to healing is a little captive girl from Israel, far from home, who wishes her master well (2 Kings 5:3).

Naaman expected a great ceremony. Elisha did not even come out; he sent word: go, wash in the Jordan seven times. Naaman was angry. Are not the rivers of Damascus better? It was his servants who said: if he had asked something difficult, you would have done it. How much more when he only says, wash, and be clean (2 Kings 5:13).

He went down, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean (2 Kings 5:14). And he said: now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. The water healed his skin; humility healed his heart.

In the Gospel the people of Nazareth could not accept Jesus because they knew him too well. He reminded them that Naaman the Syrian was cleansed when many in Israel were not (Luke 4:27). This Lent let us not wait for something grand. God heals us through simple things: water, a word of absolution, bread and wine. Let us go down into the water. Amen.
kids: Children, Naaman was a big, strong general, but he was sick. God told him: go and wash seven times in the river. He thought it was too easy and got angry! But when he obeyed, God healed him. God gave us water too, in our baptism. Let us thank Jesus for our baptism today!

homily: Dear friends, the young men in the furnace had lost everything: their land, their Temple, their sacrifices. In the fire Azariah prays: we have no place to make an offering before you and to find mercy. Yet with a contrite heart and a humble spirit may we be accepted (Daniel 3:38–39).

This is good news for us. There are days when we feel we have nothing to bring to God: no virtues, no success, only failures. God accepts that broken heart. The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit (Psalm 51:17).

But mercy received must become mercy given. Peter asks: how often should I forgive? Seven times? Jesus says: not seven times, but seventy-seven times (Matthew 18:22). Then he tells of a servant forgiven a debt he could never pay, who goes out and seizes a fellow servant by the throat over a small sum.

The king asks him: should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you? (Matthew 18:33). Each day we pray: forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us. This Lent, let us cancel one debt from the heart. It may be hard; ask for the grace, and God will give it. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter asked Jesus: how many times do I have to forgive? Jesus said: seventy-seven times! That means every time. When someone hurts you and says sorry, say: I forgive you. Jesus forgives us every time too!

homily: Dear friends, Moses says to Israel: give heed to the statutes and ordinances that I am teaching you… so that you may live (Deuteronomy 4:1). God's law is not a cage; it is the way of life.

And Moses names the real wonder: what other great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him? (Deuteronomy 4:7). The commandments are the words of a God who has come close to his people. And he adds: make them known to your children and your children's children.

Jesus says: do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). He does not cancel the commandments. He takes them to the heart, and he fulfils them by his own obedience, all the way to the cross.

Then he says: whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:19). First do, then teach. Parents, grandparents, catechists: our children learn the commandments more from our lives than from our lessons. This Lent, let us keep God's law with love and hand it on with joy. Amen.
kids: Children, God gave us his commandments like a loving father gives rules to keep his children safe and happy. Jesus kept all of God's commandments perfectly because he loved his Father. Let us learn one commandment today and keep it with love!

homily: Dear friends, God says through Jeremiah: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people (Jeremiah 7:23). But they did not listen. They looked backward rather than forward. And at the end: truth has perished; it is cut off from their lips.

The Psalm turns this into a word for us: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). A hard heart is not one that never heard God. It is one that heard him many times and stopped listening.

In the Gospel Jesus frees a man who could not speak, and some say: he does it by Beelzebul. Jesus answers: if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come to you (Luke 11:20). He is the stronger one who overpowers the strong man. And there is no neutral ground: whoever is not with me is against me.

Today we remember St Casimir, a young prince who lived among palace voices but listened to the voice of God. He prayed, he served the poor, he loved Our Lady. He died at twenty-five, faithful. Let us ask for his prayers, so that today, not tomorrow, we may hear the Lord's voice and gather with him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is stronger than anything bad. He healed a man who could not talk. Today we also remember St Casimir, a prince who loved Jesus more than his palace. Let us listen to Jesus today by saying a quiet prayer!

homily: Dear friends, at the end of the book of Hosea God himself teaches his people how to come back: take words with you and return to the LORD; say to him, take away all guilt; accept that which is good (Hosea 14:2). God does not wait with folded arms. He goes before us and puts the words of repentance in our mouths.

And he answers: I will heal their disloyalty; I will love them freely… I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily (Hosea 14:4–5). This is how God receives a sinner who returns: not with a cold welcome, but like dew on a dry garden.

In the Gospel a scribe asks: which commandment is the first of all? Jesus answers: hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength (Mark 12:29–30). And the second: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. They cannot be separated.

Jesus tells the scribe: you are not far from the kingdom of God. Not far, but not yet in. What brings us in is Jesus himself, who on the Cross loved the Father and loved us to the end. On this Friday of Lent let us stand before the Cross, take words with us, and return. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said the most important thing is to love God with all your heart, and to love other people too. God loves us so much! Today, Friday, let us look at the cross and say: Jesus, I love you with all my heart.

homily: Dear friends, the people in Hosea sing: come, let us return to the LORD; for it is he who has torn, and he will heal us (Hosea 6:1). It sounds like a perfect repentance. But God answers: your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early (Hosea 6:4). Their conversion lasted an hour.

God wants more: for I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings (Hosea 6:6). Faithful love, not religious display. Jesus repeated these words when people complained that he ate with sinners.

In the Gospel two men pray in the Temple. The Pharisee says: God, I thank you that I am not like other people… I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all my income (Luke 18:11–12). What he says is true, but he prays to a mirror. The tax collector stands far off, beats his breast, and says: God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13).

Jesus says the tax collector went down to his home justified, for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted (Luke 18:14). This weekend, let us bring that prayer to the confessional. God does not despise a broken and contrite heart. Amen.
kids: Children, two men prayed in church. One said: God, I am better than everybody! The other said: God, I am sorry, please be kind to me. God loved the humble prayer. Let us say tonight: Jesus, I am sorry, please be kind to me.

homily: Dear friends, today God speaks through Isaiah like a builder about to begin: for I am about to create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17). No more weeping, no more children dying, no more wasted work. That is where God is taking the world, and that is where Lent is taking us: to Easter, the first morning of the new creation.

In the Gospel a father comes to Jesus because his little boy is dying. Jesus says: unless you see signs and wonders you will not believe. The father does not argue; he only begs: sir, come down before my little boy dies.

And Jesus says only: go; your son will live (John 4:50). Think of that walk home. No sign, no proof, only a word. The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way. On the road the good news meets him: the fever left the boy at the very hour Jesus spoke. That is what faith is: walking on the strength of Christ's word.

Today we remember St John of God, who once lived a wild and wandering life. After his conversion he filled a house in Granada with the sick and the poor and served them with his own hands, because he saw Christ in every one of them. Let us believe the word of Jesus, and let that faith become hands that serve the sick. Amen.
kids: Children, a father's son was very sick. Jesus said: go home, your son will live! The father believed Jesus and went home, and his son was well. When Jesus says something, we can trust him. Let us pray today for a child who is sick.

homily: Dear friends, Ezekiel sees water flowing from under the door of the Temple. It grows from ankle-deep to knee-deep to a river that could not be crossed. It flows into the Dead Sea and makes it fresh: wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live (Ezekiel 47:9). That river is a picture of grace, and we first stepped into it at our Baptism.

In the Gospel there is a pool full of sick people, and one man who has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus asks him: do you want to be made well? (John 5:6). It is not a foolish question. Sometimes we grow used to our illness, our sin, our sadness, and we stop hoping.

The man answers: sir, I have no one to put me into the pool. Thirty-eight years, and no one. Then Jesus says: stand up, take your mat and walk. And he walks. Later Jesus tells him: do not sin any more. Jesus heals the body, but he wants to heal the soul even more. That is why we go to Confession in Lent.

Today we remember St Frances of Rome, a wife and mother who nursed the sick through plague and war and opened her home to the poor. She found God at the altar and in the kitchen. Let us ask Jesus to heal us, and let us become, like her, someone for those who have no one. Amen.
kids: Children, a man was sick for thirty-eight years, and he had no friend to help him. Jesus came and said: stand up and walk! And he walked. Jesus is a friend to people who are alone. Can you be a friend to someone who is alone at school?

homily: Dear friends, the exiles in Babylon said: the LORD has forsaken me, my Lord has forgotten me. Maybe you have said that too, in a hospital, at a graveside, or in a long struggle with sin.

God answers through Isaiah: can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you (Isaiah 49:15). And he adds: see, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands. On the cross those palms were pierced for us. Our names are written there.

In the Gospel Jesus says: my Father is still working, and I also am working (John 5:17). God never stops loving and giving life, and Jesus does the same works as the Father. Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whomever he wishes.

And he promises: anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life… and has passed from death to life (John 5:24). Today, let us hear his word and believe. And let us become the memory of God for someone who feels forgotten. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother never forgets her baby. God says: even if a mother forgot, I will never forget you! God has written your name on his hands. Look at your hand today and remember: God is holding you.

homily: Dear friends, at the foot of Mount Sinai the people grew impatient and made a golden calf. They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass, as the Psalm says. We laugh at them, but we do the same: we put money, success, our phones or our pride in the place of God.

God says to Moses: let me alone… and of you I will make a great nation. But Moses will not leave his people. He pleads: O LORD, why does your wrath burn hot against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt? (Exodus 32:11). Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel. And God spares them. That is the power of intercession.

Moses points to Jesus, who stands between God and us, and always lives to make intercession for us. In the Gospel Jesus says: you search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life (John 5:39–40). The Bible is not just a book to study. It is a road to a Person.
This Lent, let us break our golden calves. Let us pray for someone who has wandered, as Moses prayed, as many mothers pray. And let us open the Scriptures every day to meet Jesus there. Amen.
kids: Children, God's people made a golden statue of a calf and prayed to it instead of to God. Moses prayed for them and God forgave them. Let us pray today for someone we love, like Moses did.

homily: Dear friends, the Book of Wisdom lets us hear the thoughts of people who have decided that life ends in nothing. Their plan is simple: enjoy everything and crush anyone who gets in the way. And who gets in the way? The righteous man. Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us (Wisdom 2:12).

His goodness is a silent rebuke. So they say: let us test him with insult and torture; let us condemn him to a shameful death. When we hear these words, we see the cross. But Wisdom adds: they did not know the secret purposes of God.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches openly in the Temple. They want to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come (John 7:30). Jesus is not trapped by events. When his hour comes, he will give his life freely, out of love for us.

Today is a Friday of Lent. We keep abstinence and many of us will walk the Way of the Cross. Let us walk with him, and let us not be afraid to be inconvenient for the sake of goodness. The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit (Psalm 34:18). Amen.
kids: Children, some people did not like Jesus because he was so good. But God was always close to him. When you are sad, remember: God is close to you too. Today, Friday, let us say thank you to Jesus for loving us all the way to the cross.

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah discovers that people from his own town want to kill him. He says: I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter (Jeremiah 11:19). He does not take revenge. He says to God: to you I have committed my cause. In Jeremiah the Church sees Jesus, the true Lamb, who goes to his death without hatred.

In the Gospel the Temple police are sent to arrest Jesus. They come back with empty hands. Why? Because, they say, never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). They came to bind him, and his word bound their hearts.

Then Nicodemus, who once came to Jesus by night, speaks up. It is only a small question: our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing, does it? But it is a beginning. On Good Friday this same Nicodemus will come openly to bury Jesus with myrrh and aloes.

Next Sunday the Church enters the last two weeks of Lent. Let the word of Jesus disarm us. And let us find the courage, even a little at first, to speak for him and for those who are judged unfairly. Amen.
kids: Children, some men were sent to catch Jesus. But when they heard him speak, they could not do it! They said: no one ever spoke like him. Jesus' words are full of love. Let us listen to them carefully at Mass tomorrow.

homily: Dear friends, today we meet two women on trial. Susanna is innocent. Two elders, judges of the people, try to force her into sin and threaten to accuse her falsely if she refuses. She answers: I choose not to do it; I will fall into your hands, rather than sin in the sight of the Lord (Daniel 13:23). She would rather lose her life than lose God.

Condemned by a court that believed the elders, she prays: O eternal God, you know what is secret (Daniel 13:42). And God raises up young Daniel, who exposes the lie with one question: under what tree? The assembly blesses God, who saves those who hope in him. God sees, and God defends.

The second woman is guilty. Her accusers want to use her to trap Jesus. He writes on the ground and says: let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her (John 8:7). They go away, one by one, beginning with the eldest. Only Jesus and the woman remain: misery and mercy, as St Augustine says.

Jesus says: neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). He does not call sin nothing; he gives her a new beginning. This week, as we draw close to the cross, let us drop our stones, go to confession, and hear those same words spoken to us. Amen.
kids: Children, some people wanted to throw stones at a woman who had done wrong. Jesus said: only someone who has never sinned can throw the first stone. Nobody could! Jesus forgave her. Today, instead of saying unkind words about someone, let us say a kind word or a prayer for them.

homily: Dear friends, the people of Israel were tired of walking and tired of the manna. They said: we detest this miserable food (Numbers 21:5). The bread from heaven had become boring. Poisonous serpents came, and many died. Then they confessed: we have sinned.

God gave Moses a strange remedy: make a serpent of bronze and set it on a pole; whoever is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). The very image of what was killing them became the sign of healing, because God chose to heal through it.

Jesus told Nicodemus: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). And today he says: when you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). On the cross Jesus takes the poison of our sin into himself. And there, where he seems weakest, he is revealed as I AM, the Son of God.

Our crosses may be veiled in purple this week. On Good Friday they will be uncovered and we will be invited to look and adore. Let us begin now: look at the crucifix, bring him our wounds, stop complaining and trust. Whoever looks to him in faith will live. Amen.
kids: Children, when God's people were bitten by snakes, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake on a pole. Whoever looked at it got better! Jesus was lifted up on the cross so that everyone who looks at him with love can be healed from sin. Look at a cross today and say: thank you, Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, three young men stand before a furious king. Bow to the golden statue, or burn. They answer: if our God is able to deliver us, let him deliver us. But if not, we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:17–18). Their faith does not depend on a rescue. They will be faithful either way.

They are thrown into the furnace, and the king sees four men walking in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods. God does not always keep us out of the fire. He comes into it with us.

Jesus speaks of freedom: if you continue in my word, you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free. Everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. So if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:31–36). The worst slavery is not chains on the hands, but sin in the heart.

St Patrick knew both. Enslaved as a boy in Ireland, he found God while tending sheep in the cold. Freed, he chose to return as a bishop to the land of his slavery, to make its people free in Christ. Let us ask today for faith that does not bargain and for the freedom only the Son can give. Amen.
kids: Children, three young men would not bow down to a golden statue, because they loved God. They were thrown into a fire, but God was with them, and they came out without even the smell of smoke! St Patrick was a slave as a boy, but he became a bishop and taught Ireland about Jesus. Say today: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me!

homily: Dear friends, Abram is ninety-nine years old and has no son, and God says: you shall be the ancestor of a multitude of nations. No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham (Genesis 17:4–5). A new name means a new mission. God makes an everlasting covenant, and he never forgets it.

In the Gospel Jesus says: your ancestor Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad (John 8:56). All the promises to Abraham were looking forward to Jesus. In him the blessing reaches all nations, and we too become Abraham's children by faith and Baptism.

Then Jesus says: very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). Not I was, but I AM, the holy name of God. This is why some picked up stones. Jesus is not only a great teacher. He is the eternal Son of God, who was before Abraham and before the world.

St Cyril of Jerusalem, whom we remember today, taught this faith to those preparing for Baptism near the very place of the Cross and the empty tomb, and suffered exile to defend it. Let us renew our own baptismal faith as Easter approaches, and adore Jesus, true God and true man. Amen.
kids: Children, God gave Abram a new name, Abraham, and promised him a family as big as the stars. Jesus said something amazing: before Abraham was born, I AM. Jesus was always there, because he is God! Ask your parents today the date of your Baptism, the day you joined God's family.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the middle of Lent we put on white to honour St Joseph. In the whole Gospel he does not say a single word. Yet God entrusted to him his two greatest treasures: his only Son and the Virgin Mary.

God promised David: I will raise up your offspring after you… and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever (2 Samuel 7:12–13). A thousand years later the heir of David is a carpenter in Nazareth. Through Joseph, who gives the child his name, Jesus becomes son of David. God keeps his promises through humble people.

Joseph's world is turned upside down: Mary is with child. Being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, he planned to dismiss her quietly (Matthew 1:19). His goodness is full of mercy. But God has a bigger plan, and an angel tells him in a dream: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife (Matthew 1:20).

Then come the most beautiful words about him: when Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). No argument, no delay. Like Abraham, hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Joseph teaches us that faith is not many words, but quiet obedience.

At Nazareth Jesus went down with Mary and Joseph and was obedient to them. The Son of God learned to work with wood, to pray and to keep the law at Joseph's side. Every father, every worker, every person who cares for others in silence can look to Joseph and find his own vocation honoured.

Let us entrust ourselves today to St Joseph: our families, our work, our Church and our last hour. May he teach us to listen to God in the night, to rise, and to do what God asks. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, St Joseph was a carpenter. He took care of Jesus and Mary, kept them safe, worked hard to give them food, and taught Jesus how to make things with wood.
When God spoke to Joseph, he obeyed straight away. Today, when Mummy or Daddy asks you to do something good, do it straight away, like St Joseph!

homily: Dear friends, Ezekiel saw God's people broken into two kingdoms and scattered among the nations. And God promised: I will make them one nation… never again shall they be two nations… they shall all have one shepherd (Ezekiel 37:22, 24). God's dream is not a scattered people but one family.

In the Gospel, after Lazarus is raised, some leaders are afraid. Caiaphas says: it is better for you to have one man die for the people than to have the whole nation destroyed (John 11:50). He was thinking of politics. But John tells us he was prophesying: Jesus would die not only for the nation, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God (John 11:52).

We must hear this rightly. The Church teaches that the death of Jesus cannot be blamed on all the Jews of that time or on the Jewish people today. The deepest truth is that Jesus died for the sins of all of us, and freely gave his life. And what men intended for evil, God used for the salvation of the world.

The pilgrims in the Temple asked: will he come to the festival? Tomorrow is Palm Sunday. He comes. Let us go out to meet him with palms, and let us make peace with one another, so that he may gather us into one at his cross. Amen.
kids: Children, God wants all his children to be one big family. Jesus gave his life to bring everyone together. Tomorrow is Palm Sunday, and we will wave palms for Jesus our King! Today, if you have quarrelled with someone, go and make peace.

homily: Dear friends, Holy Week has begun, and the Church gives us the first Song of the Servant: here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him (Isaiah 42:1). This is Jesus. He does not shout in the street. A bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not quench (Isaiah 42:3). If your faith is only a flicker today, he will not blow it out. He will breathe on it.

Six days before the Passover, Jesus comes to Bethany. Martha serves, Lazarus sits at table, and Mary takes a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anoints the feet of Jesus and wipes them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume (John 12:3). That perfume was worth a year's wages. Mary does not calculate. She loves.

Judas does calculate. Why was this not sold and given to the poor? But he did not care about the poor; he was a thief. Jesus answers: leave her alone. She bought it so that she might keep it for the day of my burial (John 12:7). Mary has understood that Jesus is going to die. True love for the poor is born from love for Jesus, not opposed to it.

This week, let us not be spectators. Let us be Mary. Break the jar: give Jesus your time at the services of the Triduum, your sins in confession, your tears, your love. And when the darkness of the Passion comes, pray with the Psalm: the LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? (Psalm 27:1). Amen.
kids: Children, Mary loved Jesus so much that she poured her most precious perfume on his feet, and the whole house smelt lovely. This week, let us give Jesus something precious too: our prayers, our kindness and our hearts!

homily: Dear friends, in today's first reading the Servant speaks: the LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me (Isaiah 49:1).
