And then he admits: I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing (Isaiah 49:4). But God answers: it is too small a thing to restore only Israel; I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth (Isaiah 49:6).

In the Upper Room this light seems to be going out. Jesus is troubled in spirit and says: one of you will betray me. He gives a piece of bread, a sign of friendship, to Judas. Judas takes it and goes out. And it was night (John 13:30).

Then Peter says: I will lay down my life for you. Jesus answers: before the cock crows, you will have denied me three times (John 13:38). Two apostles fail him that night. Judas despairs; Peter weeps and returns. The difference is not that Peter's sin was small, but that Peter trusted the mercy of Jesus.

This Holy Week, do not go out into the night. Whatever you have done, come back to the light. Go to confession. Let Jesus look at you as he looked at Peter. From that weak, forgiven fisherman the light of Christ reached to the end of the earth, and it reaches you today. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter said he would never leave Jesus, but he got scared and said he did not know him. Then he was very sorry and cried, and Jesus forgave him and made him the leader of the apostles! When we do wrong, let us say sorry quickly and come back to Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, today the Servant tells us his secret: the Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens, wakens my ear to listen as those who are taught (Isaiah 50:4). Before he speaks, he listens. And because he listens, he does not turn back: I did not hide my face from insult and spitting (Isaiah 50:6).

In the Gospel Judas goes to the chief priests and asks: what will you give me if I betray him to you? They paid him thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15). The price of a slave. The Son of God, valued at thirty coins.

At the table Jesus says: one of you will betray me. And each disciple asks: surely not I, Lord? (Matthew 26:22). They do not point at each other. Each looks into his own heart. That is the question for us on this last day before the Triduum. For what price would I sell Jesus? For money? For comfort? For the approval of others?

But remember: Jesus did not curse Judas; he grieved over him and even at the table left the door open. No sin is bigger than his mercy. Tomorrow evening the Triduum begins. Let us come to it as the Servant did, with a listening ear and a face set like flint, trusting that the Lord GOD helps us. Amen.
kids: Children, Judas sold Jesus for thirty silver coins. How sad! Jesus is worth more than all the money and toys in the world. Let us tell Jesus today: you are my best friend, and I will never trade you for anything!

homily: Dear friends, the Church keeps Easter for eight whole days, because one day is not enough for so great a joy. Today Peter stands before a great crowd and says: this Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses (Acts 2:32).

Think of who is speaking. A few weeks earlier Peter denied Jesus three times. Now he speaks with boldness before thousands. What changed him? He met the risen Lord, and he received the Holy Spirit. The best proof of the Resurrection is a changed life.

Peter quotes David: you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit (Psalm 16:10). David died and his tomb was still there. But Jesus' body did not see corruption. God raised him up, because it was impossible for him to be held in death's power (Acts 2:24).

In the Gospel the women run from the tomb with fear and great joy. And suddenly Jesus meets them: greetings! They hold his feet and worship him. He says: do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers. He calls those who ran away his brothers. Easter is forgiveness.

Some tried to explain it away: the disciples stole the body while we were asleep. St Augustine laughed: if they were asleep, how did they see? People still try to explain away the Resurrection. But the truth cannot be bought.
This week, let us be like the women: running with joy, holding fast to the Lord in the Eucharist, and telling our brothers and sisters: do not be afraid, he is risen. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the women ran from the tomb so happy, and Jesus met them on the way and said: hello! Do not be afraid!
Jesus says the same to you today: do not be afraid, I am alive and I am with you. Go and tell your friends!

homily: Dear friends, on the day of Pentecost the crowd heard Peter's preaching and were cut to the heart. They asked: brothers, what should we do? Peter said: repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:37–38). That day about three thousand were baptized.

Peter's words, this Jesus whom you crucified, are spoken to each of us. Our sins too nailed him to the cross. But the One we crucified is the One who forgives. That is why the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.

In the Gospel Mary Magdalene is weeping at the tomb. Angels speak to her; Jesus himself stands before her; but she does not recognize him. She thinks he is the gardener. Sometimes we too are so full of our sorrow that we do not see the Lord standing beside us.

Then Jesus says one word: Mary! (John 20:16). Only one person says our name like that. She turns and cries: Rabbouni! At our Baptism Jesus called us by name too. He still does, in prayer, in his word, in the sacraments.
But Jesus says: do not hold on to me… go to my brothers. Mary must not keep him for herself. She goes and says: I have seen the Lord (John 20:18). She becomes the apostle to the apostles.
Today, let the Lord call you by name. Let his word cut you to the heart and heal you. And then go, like Mary, and tell someone: I have seen the Lord. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary was crying because she thought Jesus was gone. But Jesus said her name, and she knew him and became very happy!
Jesus knows your name too. Close your eyes and hear him say it with love. Then say: Jesus, I love you!

homily: Dear friends, Peter and John meet a man who has never walked in his life. He asks for a coin. Peter says: I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk (Acts 3:6). And the man goes into the Temple walking and leaping and praising God.
The Church is not rich in silver and gold; her treasure is the name of Jesus. When we give Christ, people are healed and raised up. What do you have to give today?

In the Gospel two disciples are walking away from Jerusalem, sad. They say: we had hoped (Luke 24:21). Hope in the past tense. Perhaps some of us are walking that road too, away from the Church, away from hope.

But Jesus walks with them, though they do not recognize him. He opens the Scriptures, and their hearts begin to burn. Later they say: were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road? (Luke 24:32). That is what happens when we listen to God's word.

They invite him: stay with us, because it is almost evening. At table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them, and their eyes are opened. They recognize him in the breaking of the bread. This is the Mass: the Word that sets hearts on fire, and the Bread that is the risen Lord himself.

And then they run back to Jerusalem, at night, to tell the others. That is what every Mass does to us: it sends us out. Let us ask the Lord today: stay with us, and send us to give what we have, the name of Jesus. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus were sad. Jesus walked with them, but they did not know it was him. At supper he broke the bread, and they knew: it is Jesus!
At Mass the priest breaks the bread too, and Jesus is really there. Let us say: Jesus, stay with us!

intro: Theme: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.”
Exile and homecoming, the serpent lifted up, the love that saves, and the mercy that makes us alive.

q: The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent persistently to them by his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place;
But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.
points.apply: Name one area of your life where you feel in exile from God, and bring it to him in prayer this week.

sub: The cross as the place of healing.
q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Spend five minutes before a crucifix each day this week, looking and letting yourself be healed.

sub: Not to condemn but to save.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?

For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life. Indeed, God did not send the Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.
points.apply: Bring one hidden thing into the light of confession before Holy Week.

q: He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him;
For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
points.apply: Do one good work this week as a thank-you to God, not as a payment.

concl: God's compassion has the last word over our exile.
Christ lifted up on the cross is the love of God that saves, heals and makes us alive.
2027-03-07.resolve: Learn John 3:16 by heart and pray it every morning until Easter.

intro: Theme: “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”
A covenant written on the heart, a clean heart created, the nations seeking Jesus, and the seed that dies to bear fruit.

points.h: A covenant written on the heart
sub: The cup of the new covenant.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And he did the same with the cup after supper, saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.
points.apply: At Mass this week, at the words over the chalice, renew your covenant with God in your heart.

points.h: Create in me a clean heart
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Make your Easter confession this week, before Holy Week begins.

q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and said to him, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”
points.apply: Invite one person to come with you to a Holy Week service.

q: When you make his life an offering for sin, he shall see his offspring, and shall prolong his days;
Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Offer one hidden sacrifice each day until Easter, as a grain of wheat for someone you love.

concl: God writes a new covenant on our hearts in the blood of Christ and creates in us clean hearts.
The world wishes to see Jesus, and it sees him lifted up on the cross, the grain of wheat that bears the harvest of Easter.
2027-03-14.resolve: Make a good confession before Holy Week and offer one hidden sacrifice each day until Easter.

intro: Theme: “Truly this man was God's Son!”
The humble King, the Servant who did not turn back, the cry of the forsaken Son, and the name above every name.

q: Rejoice greatly, O daughter Zion! Shout aloud, O daughter Jerusalem! Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

Then those who went ahead and those who followed were shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our ancestor David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
points.apply: Carry your palm with faith today, and welcome Jesus as King of your home.

points.h: The Servant who did not turn back
q: I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out the beard; I did not hide my face from insult and spitting.
He said, “Abba, Father, for you all things are possible; remove this cup from me; yet, not what I want, but what you want.”
points.apply: Pray the prayer of Gethsemane each night of Holy Week over the hardest thing in your life.

q: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, from the words of my groaning?
Now when the centurion, who stood facing him, saw that in this way he breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was God's Son!”
points.apply: Kneel before the crucifix on Good Friday and make the centurion's confession your own.

q: By myself I have sworn, from my mouth has gone forth in righteousness a word that shall not return: “To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.”
he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,
points.apply: Bow your head at the name of Jesus each time you hear it this week.

concl: The King hailed with palms enters Jerusalem to give his life.
Through the cross, the forsaken Son is revealed and exalted, and every knee shall bend.
2027-03-21.resolve: Keep the whole of Holy Week: the Lord's Supper, the Passion and the Easter Vigil.

intro: Theme: “Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.”
Holy Thursday: the Passover Lamb, the gift of the Eucharist, the gift of the priesthood and the towel of love.

sub: The night of liberation in Egypt.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Before Communion tonight, say slowly: Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world; have mercy on me.

sub: On the night when he was betrayed.
Bread and wine become his Body and Blood.
The sacrifice of the cross made present.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
points.apply: Stay at the place of repose tonight and adore the Lord truly present.

sub: A pure offering in every place.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering;

but he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever. Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Write a short note of thanks to a priest who has served you, and pray daily this Easter season for vocations.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight, and one for a poor or sick person during the Easter Octave.

concl: Jesus is the true Passover Lamb; he gives us his Body and Blood and the priests who offer his sacrifice.
He loves us to the end, washes our feet and sends us to love one another in the same way.
2027-03-25.resolve: Watch one hour with the Lord tonight, and take up the towel of service tomorrow.

intro: Theme: “It is finished.”
The Servant wounded for us, the King on the Cross, the fountain from his side, and the high priest who sympathizes with our weakness.

sub: By his bruises we are healed.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross, so that, free from sins, we might live for righteousness; by his wounds you have been healed.
points.apply: Look at a crucifix for five minutes today and say slowly: for me.

sub: A kingdom not from this world.
q: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, from the words of my groaning?
Pilate also had an inscription written and put on the cross. It read, “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.”
points.apply: Pray Psalm 22 today, the psalm Jesus prayed on the cross, from beginning to end.

points.h: It is finished: the fountain from his side
sub: The Church born from his heart.
q: On that day a fountain shall be opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Baptism and for every Communion you have received.

sub: Tested as we are, yet without sin.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases; yet we accounted him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.

For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Bring one burden to the Cross today and leave it there; and visit or call someone who is suffering.

concl: The Cross is not defeat but love completed: the Servant, the King and the Priest give their life for us.
No one people is to blame; all sinners caused his Passion, and all are invited to his mercy.
2027-03-26.resolve: Keep the fast, adore the Cross, and forgive one person from the heart today.

intro: Theme: “He has been raised; he is not here.”
The Easter Vigil: light in the darkness, the story of salvation, the waters of Baptism and the empty tomb.

points.h: The light that darkness cannot overcome
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
points.apply: Light a candle at home this Easter week during family prayer, and let it remind you of your baptismal candle.

sub: From creation to the new heart.
Abraham and the lamb God provides.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
Then beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them the things about himself in all the scriptures.
points.apply: Read one of the seven Vigil readings each day this Easter week.

sub: Clean water and a new heart.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you. A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Bless yourself with holy water each time you enter the church, remembering your Baptism.

sub: Go, tell his disciples and Peter.
q: But Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the LORD will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today you shall never see again.
But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed; you are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has been raised; he is not here. Look, there is the place they laid him.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, in your own words, why the Resurrection matters to you.

concl: From one flame the whole church is lit: Christ is the light of the world.
In Baptism we died and rose with him; in the Eucharist we eat the Passover of the risen Lamb.
2027-03-27.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises tonight with all your heart, and live this week as one who walks in newness of life.

intro: Theme: “He saw and believed.”
The empty tomb, the witnesses who ate with him, the life hidden with Christ, and Christ our Passover.

q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
Then the other disciple, who reached the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed;
points.apply: Go to Mass every Sunday of the Easter season as a meeting with the risen Lord, not an obligation.

points.h: Witnesses who ate and drank with him
q: I shall not die, but I shall live, and recount the deeds of the LORD.
but God raised him on the third day and allowed him to appear, not to all the people but to us who were chosen by God as witnesses, and who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
points.apply: Learn one simple way to explain the Resurrection to a friend who asks.

points.h: Seek the things that are above
sub: A life hidden with Christ in God.
q: he will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces
So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth,
points.apply: Choose one earthly worry and hand it over to God each morning this week.

sub: The bread of sincerity and truth.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.

Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed. Therefore, let us celebrate the festival, not with the old yeast, the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
points.apply: Clean out one “old yeast” this week: a grudge, a lie or a habit of malice.

concl: Christ is truly risen in his body; the tomb is empty and the witnesses ate with him.
Raised with him in Baptism and fed by him in the Eucharist, we live as an Easter people.
2027-03-28.resolve: Greet everyone this week with “Christ is risen!” and live one concrete act of Easter joy each day.

intro: Theme: “Go, wash, and be clean.”
The little captive girl, the humble waters of the Jordan, and the prophet rejected at home.

points.h: Grace begins with the little ones
sub: A great man with a hidden wound.
A captive girl who wishes her master well.
q: She said to her mistress, “If only my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy.”
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly;
points.apply: Thank God for one humble person who led you closer to him, and tell them so this week.

sub: Seven times in a muddy river.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
And this is what some of you used to be. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
points.apply: Go to confession before Holy Week and receive God's simple, powerful word of pardon.

q: As a deer longs for flowing streams, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
There were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.
points.apply: Listen this week, with an open heart, to someone whose voice you have stopped hearing.

concl: God heals the proud through humble means and humble people.
The waters of Baptism make us new, and his mercy reaches every nation.
2027-03-01.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises each morning this week with holy water.

intro: Theme: “Not seven times, but seventy-seven times.”
A contrite heart in the furnace, and the mercy that must flow on.

sub: For the sake of Abraham your beloved.
q: Be mindful of your mercy, O LORD, and of your steadfast love, for they have been from of old. Do not remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions;
God's love was revealed among us in this way: God sent his only Son into the world so that we might live through him.
points.apply: When you feel you have nothing to offer God, offer him that emptiness in prayer.

points.h: A contrite heart and a humble spirit
sub: God does not despise the broken.
q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
But he gives all the more grace; therefore it says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
points.apply: Pray Psalm 51 slowly once this week, as Azariah would have prayed it.

sub: Ten thousand talents and a hundred denarii.
q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
Should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly tonight and stop at the words “as we forgive”; name before God the person you need to forgive.

concl: God accepts a humble heart when we have nothing else to give.
The mercy we receive must become the mercy we give.
2027-03-02.resolve: Forgive one person from the heart before the end of this week.

intro: Theme: “I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.”
The law that gives life, the God who is near, and the Son who fulfils it all.

sub: Wisdom in the sight of the nations.
q: He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and ordinances to Israel. He has not dealt thus with any other nation;
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one commandment that has protected you or your family.

q: For what other great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him?
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
points.apply: Read a short passage of Scripture with your family each evening for the rest of Lent.

points.h: Not to abolish but to fulfil
sub: Not one stroke of a letter.
From the act to the heart.
q: No, the word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart for you to observe.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one “least” commandment you neglect and keep it faithfully this week.

concl: God's law is the gift of a God who is near.
Jesus fulfils it, and asks us to do and to teach.
2027-03-03.resolve: Teach one commandment to a child this week, first by keeping it yourself.

intro: Theme: “If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts.”
A people that would not listen, the finger of God, and the stronger one who sets us free.

sub: Truth cut off from the lips.
q: But this command I gave them, “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk only in the way that I command you, so that it may be well with you.”
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
points.apply: Choose one word of God you have heard often and act on it today.

q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah,
As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
points.apply: Make a daily ten-minute silence with the Gospel of the day for the rest of Lent.

q: And the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God!” But Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
points.apply: Renounce aloud, as at Baptism, one specific work of the evil one in your life, and ask Christ to free you.

concl: God speaks today; the danger is a heart that has stopped listening.
Christ, the stronger one, frees us, and calls us to gather with him.
2027-03-04.resolve: Spend ten minutes daily in silence with the Gospel until Easter.

intro: Theme: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart.”
The words of return, the dew of God's free love, and the two commandments joined at the Cross.

sub: God teaches the words of repentance.
q: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity. Take words with you and return to the LORD;
So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Write your own short act of contrition and pray it each night until Easter.

q: I will heal their disloyalty; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them. I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily, he shall strike root like the forests of Lebanon.
We love because he first loved us.
points.apply: Notice one sign of new growth God has given you this Lent and thank him for it.

sub: All your heart, soul, mind and strength.
q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Pray the Way of the Cross today, and at each station name one neighbour to love better.

concl: God himself teaches us to return, and receives us like dew on a dry garden.
At the Cross the love of God and the love of neighbour become one.
2027-03-05.resolve: Make one concrete act of love for God and one for a neighbour each day this week.

intro: Theme: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
Love like the morning dew, the steadfast love God desires, and the prayer that justifies.

sub: On the third day he will raise us up.
q: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Choose one Lenten resolution that has faded since Ash Wednesday and begin it again today.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.
points.apply: Do one act of mercy this weekend for someone others look down on.

q: For thus says the high and lofty one who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with those who are contrite and humble in spirit,
I tell you, this man went down to his home justified rather than the other; for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: Go to confession this weekend, and begin with the tax collector's words.

concl: God desires faithful love, not display.
The humble prayer of a sinner is heard, and he goes home justified.
2027-03-06.resolve: Pray the Jesus Prayer several times each day until Easter.

intro: Theme: “Go; your son will live.”
God makes all things new, a father believes the word of Jesus, and a saint turns faith into care for the sick.

q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.
And the one who was seated on the throne said, “See, I am making all things new.”
points.apply: Bring to God in prayer one situation that seems hopeless, and ask him to make it new.

sub: A word instead of a sign.
q: O LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.
Jesus said to him, “Go; your son will live.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way.
points.apply: Each morning this week, read one verse of the Gospel and act on it before evening.

q: You have turned my mourning into dancing; you have taken off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,
I was naked and you gave me clothing, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me.
points.apply: Visit one sick or housebound person before Sunday, and bring them Christ's peace.

concl: God is making all things new, and Easter is the first morning.
We believe the word of Jesus and walk on it, and our faith becomes care for the sick.
2027-03-08.resolve: Visit or call one sick person this week, and pray with them.

intro: Theme: “Do you want to be made well?”
The river from the Temple, the man who had no one, and a saint who carried others to the water.

q: Wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish, once these waters reach there. It will become fresh; and everything will live where the river goes.
Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises in your own words before the crucifix tonight.

points.h: Do you want to be made well?
q: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy habitation of the Most High.
When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been there a long time, he said to him, “Do you want to be made well?”
points.apply: Name the sin you have grown used to, and bring it to Confession this Lent.

sub: Frances of Rome: altar and kitchen.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
points.apply: Choose one lonely person and stay close to them for the rest of Lent.

concl: The river of grace flows from Christ, the true Temple, and makes the dead live.
Jesus asks if we want healing, and sends us to those who have no one.
2027-03-09.resolve: Help one person who has no one, every week until Easter.

intro: Theme: “Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.”
God's mother-love, the Son who works with the Father, and the voice that calls us from death to life.

q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
But even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.
points.apply: When fear says you are forgotten, pray Isaiah 49:15 slowly three times.

sub: The sabbath and the works of God.
The Son equal to the Father.
q: The LORD is good to all, and his compassion is over all that he has made.
But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, and I also am working.”
points.apply: Each evening this week, name one place where you saw God at work that day.

q: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
points.apply: Pray for one person who has died, and for one who is far from God, that both may hear the voice of the Son.

concl: God's love is stronger than a mother's and never forgets.
The Son gives life now and will raise the dead; we hear his word and live.
2027-03-10.resolve: Be the memory of God for one forgotten person this week.

intro: Theme: “It is they that testify on my behalf.”
The golden calf, Moses in the breach, and the Scriptures that lead us to Christ.

q: They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
points.apply: Fast this week from the thing that most often takes God's place in your day.

q: But Moses implored the LORD his God, and said, “O LORD, why does your wrath burn hot against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Write the names of three people far from God and pray for them every day until Easter.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
You search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day each morning this week, and end with a short prayer to Jesus.

concl: God's people fell into idolatry, and Moses' prayer saved them.
Christ is the eternal intercessor, and all the Scriptures lead to him.
2027-03-11.resolve: Pray daily for three people far from God until Easter.

intro: Theme: “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.”
The inconvenient righteous one, the hour in the Father's hands, and God's closeness in suffering.

q: Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our actions; he reproaches us for sins against the law, and accuses us of sins against our training.
“If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.
points.apply: Do one right thing this week that you have been avoiding because it is unpopular.

points.h: His hour had not yet come
sub: They know his village, not his Father.
q: My times are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and persecutors.
Then they tried to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
points.apply: Each night this week, place tomorrow in the Father's hands with Psalm 31:15.

q: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
But rejoice insofar as you are sharing Christ's sufferings, so that you may also be glad and shout for joy when his glory is revealed.
points.apply: Pray the Way of the Cross this Friday and offer it for someone who is brokenhearted.

concl: The righteous one is hated for his goodness, but the plot of the wicked does not know God's purpose.
Jesus goes to his hour freely, and God is near to all who suffer with him.
2027-03-12.resolve: Pray the Way of the Cross every Friday until Good Friday.

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
The gentle lamb, the word that disarms, and the small courage of Nicodemus.

q: But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Give one hurt you carry to God tonight, and pray for the one who caused it.

points.h: Never has anyone spoken like this
q: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read one chapter of John's Gospel slowly each day until Palm Sunday.

q: God is my shield, who saves the upright in heart.
Nicodemus, who had at first come to Jesus by night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about a hundred pounds.
points.apply: Say one word for Christ or for fairness this week where you would normally stay silent.

concl: Jeremiah, the gentle lamb, points to Christ the Lamb of God.
The word of Jesus disarms hearts, and small courage grows into faithful love.
2027-03-13.resolve: Speak one honest word for Christ or for justice this week.

intro: Theme: “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
The innocent defended, the guilty forgiven, the stones dropped.

sub: Fear God, not those who kill the body.
q: I choose not to do it; I will fall into your hands, rather than sin in the sight of the Lord.
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
points.apply: Where you are under pressure to do wrong, say no today and tell God you trust him with the cost.

points.h: The God who sees in secret
q: O eternal God, you know what is secret and are aware of all things before they come to be;
And before him no creature is hidden, but all are naked and laid bare to the eyes of the one to whom we must render an account.
points.apply: Refuse to pass on any story about another person that you have not seen for yourself.

sub: Not condemned, but sent to sin no more.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live;

Jesus straightened up and said to her, “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” She said, “No one, sir.” And Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
points.apply: Go to confession before Holy Week, and leave behind the sin Jesus names in your heart.

concl: God defends those who hope in him and forgives those who come to him.
Only the hard heart with a stone in its hand keeps itself away from mercy.
2027-03-15.resolve: Say no unkind word about anyone this week, and make your Easter confession.

intro: Theme: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.”
From the serpent on the pole to the Son on the cross: look and live.

q: The people spoke against God and against Moses, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and we detest this miserable food.”
And do not complain as some of them did, and were destroyed by the destroyer.
points.apply: Turn every complaint today into a prayer of thanks or of trust.

sub: Healing through the image of the wound.
q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Pray for five minutes before a crucifix each day of Holy Week.

q: God said to Moses, “I am who I am.”
So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.”
points.apply: On Good Friday, come to venerate the Cross, and tell Jesus in your own words that you believe he is the Son of God.

concl: God heals through what is lifted up before our eyes.
On the cross Jesus is revealed as the Son, and whoever looks to him in faith lives.
2027-03-16.resolve: Look at the crucifix each day this week and pray: Jesus, you are he; heal me.

intro: Theme: “If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.”
Faith that does not bargain, God in the fire, and the freedom of the Son; St Patrick.

sub: Faith that does not depend on rescue.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than any human authority.
points.apply: Name one idol you bow to, and refuse it this week for the love of God.

points.h: The fourth man in the fire
sub: God with us in the furnace.
q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: In your present trial, pray each day: Lord, walk with me in this fire.

points.h: The truth will make you free
q: I shall walk at liberty, for I have sought your precepts.
So if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
points.apply: Bring your heaviest chain to confession before Easter, and let the Son set you free.

concl: The three young men and St Patrick served God whether or not they were spared.
The Son of God walks with us in the fire and makes us free indeed.
2027-03-17.resolve: Pray St Patrick's Breastplate each morning of Holy Week.

intro: Theme: “Before Abraham was, I am.”
The covenant with Abraham, the joy of seeing Christ's day, and the eternal Son; St Cyril of Jerusalem.

sub: A new name, a new mission.
q: No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you the ancestor of a multitude of nations.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises in your own words tonight before you sleep.

sub: He remembers for a thousand generations.
q: I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your offspring after you throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.
Thus he has shown the mercy promised to our ancestors, and has remembered his holy covenant, the oath that he swore to our ancestor Abraham,
points.apply: Pray the Benedictus (Luke 1:68–79) in the morning this week, thanking God who keeps his covenant.

sub: Not I was, but I AM.
The stones and the hidden Lord.
Cyril's faith in the divinity of Christ.
q: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever you had formed the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
points.apply: Make a slow genuflection before the tabernacle each time you enter church this week, adoring the I AM.

concl: God's covenant with Abraham is everlasting, and in Christ we are its heirs.
Jesus is the eternal Son, the I AM, whom St Cyril taught and defended.
2027-03-18.resolve: Find the date of your Baptism and keep it this year as a day of thanksgiving.

intro: Theme: “When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him.”
The son of David, the righteous man, the faith of Abraham, and the guardian of the Redeemer.

q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.

But just when he had resolved to do this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Thank God this week for the people through whom his promises reached you: parents, godparents, teachers.

q: The righteous walk in integrity, happy are the children who follow them!
Her husband Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.
points.apply: Where someone has failed or shamed you, choose Joseph's way: protect their dignity and seek God's light.

q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become “the father of many nations,”
points.apply: Bring your most hopeless situation to St Joseph in prayer each day this week.

q: Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.”
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.
points.apply: Consecrate your family to St Joseph tonight, and pray for the dying.

concl: God fulfilled his promise to David through the silent faithfulness of Joseph.
Joseph listened, rose and obeyed, and he still guards the Church as he guarded Jesus and Mary.
2027-03-19.resolve: Do at once the one thing God has been asking of you, and entrust your family to St Joseph.

intro: Theme: “To gather into one the dispersed children of God.”
Ezekiel's promise, Caiaphas' unwitting prophecy, and the threshold of Holy Week.

q: My servant David shall be king over them; and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall follow my ordinances and be careful to observe my statutes.
I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also, and they will listen to my voice. So there will be one flock, one shepherd.
points.apply: Pray this week for Christian unity, and greet a Christian of another Church with warmth.

sub: A prophecy of salvation, and the death Christ freely accepted for all.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.

He did not say this on his own, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God.
points.apply: Say each day of Holy Week: Jesus, you died for me; gather me into your one family.

points.h: Will he come to the festival?
sub: He comes, to give his life.
q: Rejoice greatly, O daughter Zion! Shout aloud, O daughter Jerusalem! Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
They were looking for Jesus and were asking one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the festival, will he?”
points.apply: Come to the Palm Sunday procession tomorrow, and keep the whole of Holy Week with Jesus.

concl: God's will is to gather his scattered children into one.
Jesus comes to Jerusalem freely, to die for all and to make us one.
2027-03-20.resolve: Make peace with one person before Palm Sunday.

intro: Theme: “The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.”
The gentle Servant, the extravagant love of Mary, the calculating heart and the light that overcomes darkness.

sub: Chosen and upheld by the Father.
The bruised reed and the dimly burning wick.
q: a bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice.
“Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Bring your weakest point to Jesus in confession this week and let him breathe on the flickering wick.

q: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Mary took a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
points.apply: Give Jesus one costly gift this week: your full presence at the Holy Thursday, Good Friday and Easter Vigil services.

sub: Concern for the poor as a mask.
True love for the poor flows from love for Jesus.
q: I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.
and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
points.apply: Set aside what you save during Holy Week and give it quietly to the poor.

q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
points.apply: Pray Psalm 27 each night of Holy Week before you sleep.

concl: The Servant is gentle with our weakness and gives himself completely.
Mary shows us how to love him: without counting, before the cross and beyond it.
2027-03-22.resolve: Break one alabaster jar for Jesus this week, and give him the whole Triduum.

intro: Theme: “I will give you as a light to the nations.”
The Servant called from the womb, the night of Judas and the tears of Peter.

q: The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
and it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for your own call, and offer him one work that seems to have failed.

sub: Salvation to the end of the earth.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
For so the Lord has commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’
points.apply: Pray and give something this week for the missions.

sub: The night of a heart that refuses the light.
q: Even my bosom friend in whom I trusted, who ate of my bread, has lifted the heel against me.
So, after receiving the piece of bread, he immediately went out. And it was night.
points.apply: Bring into the light of confession the sin you most want to hide.

sub: I will lay down my life.
The look of Jesus and the way back.
q: For you, O Lord, are my hope, my trust, O LORD, from my youth.

“Simon, Simon, listen! Satan has demanded to sift all of you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
points.apply: Make your confession before the Triduum, and trust his mercy more than your strength.

concl: The Servant's apparent failure becomes the light of the world.
Judas and Peter both fail; mercy is refused by one and received by the other.
2027-03-23.resolve: Choose Peter's tears, not Judas's night: go to confession before Holy Thursday.

intro: Theme: “The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced.”
The listening Servant, the face like flint, the thirty pieces of silver and the humble question of the disciple.

q: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word.

“Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Begin each day of the Triduum with ten minutes of silent listening to the Word.

sub: He did not hide his face.
q: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;

looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the sake of the joy that was set before him endured the cross, disregarding its shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of God.
points.apply: When you are insulted this week, keep silence and pray for the one who insulted you.

sub: For what do I sell him?
q: So they weighed out as my wages thirty shekels of silver.
“What will you give me if I betray him to you?” They paid him thirty pieces of silver.
points.apply: Name the price for which you are tempted to betray Jesus, and renounce it in confession.

q: Insults have broken my heart, so that I am in despair. I looked for pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
And they became greatly distressed and began to say to him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”
points.apply: Enter the Triduum in humility: ask Jesus to keep you faithful, and trust his mercy if you fall.

concl: The Servant listens, suffers and trusts; he does not turn back.
Judas sold him; we ask humbly, Surely not I, Lord?, and run to his mercy.
2027-03-24.resolve: Prepare the Triduum: confession, the family timetable, and the Good Friday fast.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers.”
Not abandoned to the grave, fear and great joy, and the truth that cannot be bought.

sub: Christ whom death could not hold.
q: For you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.
But God raised him up, having freed him from death, because it was impossible for him to be held in its power.
points.apply: Pray Psalm 16 slowly each morning of this Octave.

q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
So they left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy, and ran to tell his disciples.
points.apply: Spend a few minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, worshipping the risen Lord as the women did.

sub: Faith that is not in vain.
q: I keep the LORD always before me; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation has been in vain and your faith has been in vain.
points.apply: When someone mocks the Resurrection, answer gently and with your own witness, without anger.

concl: God raised Jesus; death could not hold him, and his witnesses were transformed.
The risen Lord meets us on the road and sends us to our brothers and sisters.
2027-03-29.resolve: Tell one person each day of this Octave that Christ is risen.

intro: Theme: “Mary!” “Rabbouni!”
Cut to the heart and baptized, called by name, and sent to announce: I have seen the Lord.

sub: The promise for all who are far away.
q: Truly the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love,
Peter said to them, “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Make a good confession during the Easter season if you have not done so, and renew your baptismal promises in prayer.

sub: The gardener of the new creation.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
points.apply: Pray today using your baptismal name: “Lord, here I am, you have called me.”

q: when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
points.apply: Share with one person this week how you have met the risen Lord.

concl: The word of the Resurrection cuts to the heart and leads to Baptism and the Spirit.
The risen Lord calls each of us by name and sends us to announce him.
2027-03-30.resolve: Thank God for your Baptism today, and tell someone: I have seen the Lord.

intro: Theme: “They recognized him in the breaking of the bread.”
What I have I give you, hearts burning on the road, and the Lord known at table.

points.h: What I have I give you
sub: Walking and leaping and praising God.
q: then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.”
points.apply: Give one person today something better than money: your time, your attention, and a prayer in Jesus' name.

sub: The stranger who explains the Scriptures.
Slow of heart, set on fire.
q: Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart; for I am called by your name, O LORD, God of hosts.
They said to each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road, while he was opening the scriptures to us?”
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel before going to Mass this week, and listen for the word that sets your heart on fire.

points.h: Known in the breaking of bread
q: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his presence continually.
Then they told what had happened on the road, and how he had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
points.apply: At your next Communion, say silently: “Stay with me, Lord,” and then go and serve someone that same day.

concl: The risen Lord heals through his Church and walks with us in our disappointments.
He sets our hearts on fire with his word and gives himself in the breaking of the bread.
2027-03-31.resolve: Pray each evening of this Octave: “Stay with us, Lord, because it is almost evening.”
